-{"content": "# Workflow: Result Pipeline\n\nScore submission through verification, approval, and standings integration.\nEnsures match results are reviewed before becoming official.\n\n## Overview\n\nAfter a match is played and scores are entered, the result must pass through a\nformal review pipeline before it counts toward official standings. This prevents\ndata-entry errors and disputed scores from corrupting competition tables.\n\n## Modules Involved\n\n| Module | Role |\n|--------|------|\n| `sports_federation_result_control` | Result state machine, verification, approval |\n| `sports_federation_tournament` | Match model (base for result fields) |\n| `sports_federation_standings` | Standings computation using approved results |\n| `sports_federation_governance` | Override requests for disputed results |\n| `sports_federation_notifications` | Validator activities and club / manager notifications |\n| `sports_federation_public_site` | Publishing approved results publicly |\n| `mail` | Chatter audit trail on matches |\n\n## Verified UI navigation\n\nBackend users open **Federation → Planning → Advanced Records → Matches**. Club representatives use **My Account → Results**. Standings are under **Federation → Publication → Standings**. Result Control adds buttons to the match form; it does not add a separate Results menu.\n\n## Step-by-Step Flow\n\n### 1. Score Entry\n\n**Actor**: Federation staff or match official\n**Module**: `sports_federation_tournament`\n\n1. Open the match record after the game concludes.\n2. Enter `home_score` and `away_score`.\n3. Set match state to `done`.\n\nAt this point the result is entered but **not yet official**.\n\n### 2. Result Submission\n\n**Actor**: Federation staff\n**Module**: `sports_federation_result_control`\n\n1. Click **Submit Result** on the match form.\n2. `result_state` transitions from `draft` → `submitted`.\n3. `result_submitted_by_id` and `result_submitted_on` are recorded automatically.\n4. The submitted result remains on the match record and is ready for users in the Result Verifier group.\n5. A todo activity is created for each user in the Result Verifier group.\n\n### 3. Result Verification\n\n**Actor**: Result Verifier (security group)\n**Module**: `sports_federation_result_control`\n\n1. Verifier reviews the submitted result.\n2. Cross-checks against match sheet records, referee reports, and incident logs.\n3. Click **Verify Result**.\n4. `result_state` transitions from `submitted` → `verified`.\n5. `result_verified_by_id` and `result_verified_on` are recorded.\n6. The verifier cannot verify their own submission.\n\n### 4. Result Approval\n\n**Actor**: Result Approver (security group)\n**Module**: `sports_federation_result_control`\n\n1. Approver reviews the verified result.\n2. Click **Approve Result**.\n3. `result_state` transitions from `verified` → `approved`.\n4. `result_approved_by_id` and `result_approved_on` are recorded.\n5. `include_in_official_standings` is set to `True`.\n6. Any non-frozen standings linked to the same tournament, stage, or group are recomputed automatically.\n7. The approver must be different from both the submitter and the verifier for the same result.\n8. Approved scores are treated as immutable until the result leaves the approved state.\n9. Home and away team / club contacts receive an approval email with the official scoreline.\n10. Match forms now surface a direct tournament handoff after verification,\n    approval, contest, or correction so staff can move immediately into\n    standings review and publication follow-up.\n\nThe result is now **official** and eligible for standings computation.\n\n### 5. Contest (Exception Path)\n\n**Actor**: Club representative or federation official\n**Module**: `sports_federation_result_control`\n\n1. If a party disputes the result, click **Contest Result**.\n2. `result_state` transitions to `contested`.\n3. `result_contest_reason` is filled in with the dispute justification.\n4. The result is removed from official standings immediately\n   (`include_in_official_standings = False`), and linked non-frozen standings\n   are recomputed automatically.\n5. Home and away team / club contacts plus federation managers receive a contest notification.\n\n### 6. Correction (Exception Path)\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_result_control`, `sports_federation_governance`\n\n1. After review of the contest, the result may be corrected.\n2. Update scores if needed.\n3. Click **Correct Result**.\n4. `result_state` transitions to `corrected`.\n5. `result_correction_reason` is recorded.\n6. A governance override request may be filed for audit purposes.\n7. The corrected result stays out of official standings until it is edited,\n   re-submitted, and approved through the pipeline again.\n8. If staff need a clean restart, an approver can reset the corrected or contested result back to `draft` before re-submission.\n\nEvery transition is also written to `federation.match.result.audit`, so dispute\nhistory is preserved even after the current `result_state` moves on.\n\n### 7. Standings Update\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_standings`\n\n1. Open the relevant standings record (tournament, stage, or group level).\n2. **Recompute standings** — only results with `include_in_official_standings = True`\n   are included. Approval adds a result; contest, correction, and reset remove\n   it again until it returns to `approved`.\n3. Points are calculated using the rule set (win/draw/loss values).\n4. Tie-break rules are applied in sequence order.\n5. Standings records use `draft` → `computed` → `frozen`. Public visibility is\n   controlled separately through `website_published`.\n6. Standings forms now explain whether approved results are still missing or\n   whether the next task is website publication.\n\n### 8. Publication\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_public_site`\n\n1. Publish the standings record (`website_published = True`).\n2. If the tournament has `show_public_results = True`, individual match results\n   appear on the public tournament page.\n3. The tournament Website tab now shows whether standings are missing,\n   unpublished, or hidden behind the tournament visibility toggles, with a\n   direct link back to the standings list when operators need to act there.\n4. Public pages update to reflect the latest approved data.\n\n## State Diagram\n\n```\nResult: draft → submitted → verified → approved\n                                        → contested → corrected\n                                                    → submitted\n\nStandings: draft → computed → frozen\n```\n\n## Security Model\n\n| Group | Permissions |\n|-------|-------------|\n| Federation Staff | Submit results |\n| Result Verifier | Verify submitted results |\n| Result Approver | Approve verified results |\n\nEach step requires a different security group, enforcing **separation of duties**.\nThe workflow is intentionally defensive: submitters cannot self-verify, and approvers cannot approve their own submissions or the result they verified.\n\n## Audit Trail\n\nEvery state transition is recorded with:\n- **Who**: user ID of the person performing the action\n- **When**: datetime timestamp\n- **What**: Odoo chatter log entry on the match record\n\n## Related Workflows\n\n- [Match Day Operations](WORKFLOW_MATCH_DAY_OPERATIONS.md) — score entry context\n- [Tournament Lifecycle](WORKFLOW_TOURNAMENT_LIFECYCLE.md) — standings in tournament context\n- [Governance Override](WORKFLOW_GOVERNANCE_OVERRIDE.md) — contested result escalation\n", "content_length": 7471, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "_workflows/WORKFLOW_RESULT_PIPELINE.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "d68963c10b29e838e16de19d71464cb41d5c1fdd6b639ec9744bebbadf0375fd", "size_bytes": 7517}

+{"content": "# Workflow: Result Pipeline\n\nScore submission through verification, approval, and standings integration.\nEnsures match results are reviewed before becoming official.\n\n## Overview\n\nAfter a match is played and scores are entered, the result must pass through a\nformal review pipeline before it counts toward official standings. This prevents\ndata-entry errors and disputed scores from corrupting competition tables.\n\n## Modules Involved\n\n| Module | Role |\n|--------|------|\n| `sports_federation_result_control` | Result state machine, verification, approval |\n| `sports_federation_tournament` | Match model (base for result fields) |\n| `sports_federation_standings` | Standings computation using approved results |\n| `sports_federation_governance` | Override requests for disputed results |\n| `sports_federation_notifications` | Validator activities and club / manager notifications |\n| `sports_federation_public_site` | Publishing approved results publicly |\n| `mail` | Chatter audit trail on matches |\n\n## Verified UI navigation\n\nBackend users open **Federation → Planning → Advanced Records → Matches**. Club representatives use **My Account → Results**. Standings are under **Federation → Publishing → Standings**. Result Control adds buttons to the match form; it does not add a separate Results menu.\n\n## Step-by-Step Flow\n\n### 1. Score Entry\n\n**Actor**: Federation staff or match official\n**Module**: `sports_federation_tournament`\n\n1. Open the match record after the game concludes.\n2. Enter `home_score` and `away_score`.\n3. Set match state to `done`.\n\nAt this point the result is entered but **not yet official**.\n\n### 2. Result Submission\n\n**Actor**: Federation staff\n**Module**: `sports_federation_result_control`\n\n1. Click **Submit Result** on the match form.\n2. `result_state` transitions from `draft` → `submitted`.\n3. `result_submitted_by_id` and `result_submitted_on` are recorded automatically.\n4. The submitted result remains on the match record and is ready for users in the Result Verifier group.\n5. A todo activity is created for each user in the Result Verifier group.\n\n### 3. Result Verification\n\n**Actor**: Result Verifier (security group)\n**Module**: `sports_federation_result_control`\n\n1. Verifier reviews the submitted result.\n2. Cross-checks against match sheet records, referee reports, and incident logs.\n3. Click **Verify Result**.\n4. `result_state` transitions from `submitted` → `verified`.\n5. `result_verified_by_id` and `result_verified_on` are recorded.\n6. The verifier cannot verify their own submission.\n\n### 4. Result Approval\n\n**Actor**: Result Approver (security group)\n**Module**: `sports_federation_result_control`\n\n1. Approver reviews the verified result.\n2. Click **Approve Result**.\n3. `result_state` transitions from `verified` → `approved`.\n4. `result_approved_by_id` and `result_approved_on` are recorded.\n5. `include_in_official_standings` is set to `True`.\n6. Any non-frozen standings linked to the same tournament, stage, or group are recomputed automatically.\n7. The approver must be different from both the submitter and the verifier for the same result.\n8. Approved scores are treated as immutable until the result leaves the approved state.\n9. Home and away team / club contacts receive an approval email with the official scoreline.\n10. Match forms now surface a direct tournament handoff after verification,\n    approval, contest, or correction so staff can move immediately into\n    standings review and publication follow-up.\n\nThe result is now **official** and eligible for standings computation.\n\n### 5. Contest (Exception Path)\n\n**Actor**: Club representative or federation official\n**Module**: `sports_federation_result_control`\n\n1. If a party disputes the result, click **Contest Result**.\n2. `result_state` transitions to `contested`.\n3. `result_contest_reason` is filled in with the dispute justification.\n4. The result is removed from official standings immediately\n   (`include_in_official_standings = False`), and linked non-frozen standings\n   are recomputed automatically.\n5. Home and away team / club contacts plus federation managers receive a contest notification.\n\n### 6. Correction (Exception Path)\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_result_control`, `sports_federation_governance`\n\n1. After review of the contest, the result may be corrected.\n2. Update scores if needed.\n3. Click **Correct Result**.\n4. `result_state` transitions to `corrected`.\n5. `result_correction_reason` is recorded.\n6. A governance override request may be filed for audit purposes.\n7. The corrected result stays out of official standings until it is edited,\n   re-submitted, and approved through the pipeline again.\n8. If staff need a clean restart, an approver can reset the corrected or contested result back to `draft` before re-submission.\n\nEvery transition is also written to `federation.match.result.audit`, so dispute\nhistory is preserved even after the current `result_state` moves on.\n\n### 7. Standings Update\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_standings`\n\n1. Open the relevant standings record (tournament, stage, or group level).\n2. **Recompute standings** — only results with `include_in_official_standings = True`\n   are included. Approval adds a result; contest, correction, and reset remove\n   it again until it returns to `approved`.\n3. Points are calculated using the rule set (win/draw/loss values).\n4. Tie-break rules are applied in sequence order.\n5. Standings records use `draft` → `computed` → `frozen`. Public visibility is\n   controlled separately through `website_published`.\n6. Standings forms now explain whether approved results are still missing or\n   whether the next task is website publication.\n\n### 8. Publication\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_public_site`\n\n1. Publish the standings record (`website_published = True`).\n2. If the tournament has `show_public_results = True`, individual match results\n   appear on the public tournament page.\n3. The tournament Website tab now shows whether standings are missing,\n   unpublished, or hidden behind the tournament visibility toggles, with a\n   direct link back to the standings list when operators need to act there.\n4. Public pages update to reflect the latest approved data.\n\n## State Diagram\n\n```\nResult: draft → submitted → verified → approved\n                                        → contested → corrected\n                                                    → submitted\n\nStandings: draft → computed → frozen\n```\n\n## Security Model\n\n| Group | Permissions |\n|-------|-------------|\n| Federation Staff | Submit results |\n| Result Verifier | Verify submitted results |\n| Result Approver | Approve verified results |\n\nEach step requires a different security group, enforcing **separation of duties**.\nThe workflow is intentionally defensive: submitters cannot self-verify, and approvers cannot approve their own submissions or the result they verified.\n\n## Audit Trail\n\nEvery state transition is recorded with:\n- **Who**: user ID of the person performing the action\n- **When**: datetime timestamp\n- **What**: Odoo chatter log entry on the match record\n\n## Related Workflows\n\n- [Match Day Operations](WORKFLOW_MATCH_DAY_OPERATIONS.md) — score entry context\n- [Tournament Lifecycle](WORKFLOW_TOURNAMENT_LIFECYCLE.md) — standings in tournament context\n- [Governance Override](WORKFLOW_GOVERNANCE_OVERRIDE.md) — contested result escalation\n", "content_length": 7470, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "_workflows/WORKFLOW_RESULT_PIPELINE.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "18d8133caabdcc13757e8ad230922b5fa8d637dcded552b4393684f72900f260", "size_bytes": 7516}

Minor changes (e.g. adding a new player mid-season) require temporarily setting\n   the roster back to `draft`, making changes, re-running the readiness check, and\n   re-activating.\n2. The re-activation creates a new audit log entry recording the responsible user\n   and timestamp.\n\n### 5. Match Sheet Creation\n\n**Actor**: Club administrator / team manager\n**Module**: `sports_federation_rosters`\n\n1. For each fixture, create a **match sheet** (`federation.match.sheet`) linked to\n   the match, the team, and the source roster.\n2. Set the **side** (home / away / other).\n3.  {"content": "# Workflow: Standings Lifecycle\n\nAutomatic and manual standing recomputation, freeze points, website\npublication, and the impact of official-result changes on standings tables.\n\n## Overview\n\nStandings are derived from results that still have\n`include_in_official_standings = True`. They recompute automatically when a\nresult becomes official, can be recomputed manually at any time, and are\nfrozen when the authoritative ranking for a stage must be locked. Public\nvisibility is separate from the standings state itself and is controlled\nthrough `website_published`.\n\n## Modules Involved\n\n| Module | Role |\n|--------|------|\n| `sports_federation_standings` | Standings model, recompute engine |\n| `sports_federation_result_control` | Result approval triggering recompute |\n| `sports_federation_tournament` | Tournament, stage, match records |\n| `sports_federation_governance` | Override requests for disputed standings |\n| `sports_federation_public_site` | Publication (`website_published`) |\n| `sports_federation_notifications` | Notification on standings publication |\n\n## Models\n\n| Model | Key Fields |\n|-------|-----------|\n| `federation.standings` | `tournament_id`, `stage_id`, `group_id`, `state`, `computed_on`, `website_published`, `public_title` |\n| `federation.standings.line` | `team_id`, `position`, `points`, `played`, `won`, `drawn`, `lost`, `goals_for`, `goals_against`, `goal_diff` |\n\n## Standing States\n\n```\ndraft → computed → frozen\n```\n\n| State | Meaning |\n|-------|---------|\n| `draft` | Standings record exists but has not been computed |\n| `computed` | Standings are up to date with the currently official results |\n| `frozen` | Standings are locked; no further recompute will change them |\n\n`website_published = True` controls whether the standing is visible on the\npublic site. It does not create a separate standings workflow state.\n\n## Step-by-Step Flow\n\n### 1. Automatic Recompute Trigger\n\n**Actor**: System (triggered by result approval)\n**Module**: `sports_federation_result_control` → `sports_federation_standings`\n\nWhen a match result is approved (`result_state = approved`):\n\n1. `include_in_official_standings` is set to `True` on the match record.\n2. The result approval method calls\n   `federation.standings._trigger_recompute(tournament_id, stage_id, group_id)`.\n3. Any `federation.standings` record linked to the same tournament / stage /\n   group that is in `draft` or `computed` state is queued for recompute.\n4. The standings table is rebuilt from scratch from all approved results\n   in that scope.\n5. After recompute, the standings transition to `computed`.\n\n**Frozen standings are not recomputed**. If a result is approved after the\nstandings have been frozen, a warning appears on the match form but the\nstandings are not changed.\n\n### 2. Manual Recompute\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_standings`\n\nWhen results are corrected or the automatic trigger did not fire (e.g. an edge\ncase during bulk import):\n\n1. Navigate to **Federation → Standings** and open the relevant standings record.\n2. Click **Recompute** (only available in `draft` or `computed` states, never on\n   `frozen` or `published`).\n3. The standings engine rebuilds all lines from approved results.\n4. State transitions to `computed`.\n\n### 3. Freeze Decision\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator (Federation Manager group)\n**Module**: `sports_federation_standings`\n\nStandings are frozen at a natural boundary — end of group stage, end of regular\nseason, or after the last knockout round of a stage:\n\n1. Open the standings record in `computed` state.\n2. Click **Freeze**.\n3. State transitions: `computed → frozen`.\n4. Frozen standings will not be touched by any subsequent result approval in\n   that scope.\n\n**Who can freeze**: only users in the `group_federation_manager` security group\ncan freeze standings.\n\n**When to freeze**: freeze only after all matches in the stage are `done` and\nall results are `approved`. Freezing with unapproved results creates an\nincomplete official table.\n\n### 4. Publication Approval\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_standings` → `sports_federation_public_site`\n\nBefore standings appear on the public website, a publication approval step\nprovides a human review checkpoint:\n\n1. With standings in `computed` or `frozen` state, publish the record from the\n   Website tab.\n2. `website_published` is set to `True`.\n3. The standings page at `/competitions/<edition-slug>/standings` now reflects the\n   table.\n\nIf `sports_federation_notifications` is installed, a notification is dispatched\nto club contacts when standings for their tournament are published.\n\n**Unpublishing**: set `website_published = False` to pull the standings from\nthe public site without changing the `state`. This is useful when a dispute or\nlate correction requires re-review.\n\n### 5. Contested Result Impact on Standings\n\n**Actor**: Club representative or federation official → Governance officer\n**Module**: `sports_federation_result_control` + `sports_federation_governance`\n\nWhen a result is contested after standings have been computed:\n\n1. `result_state` moves to `contested` and\n   `include_in_official_standings` becomes `False`.\n2. Any standings in `draft` or `computed` scope are recomputed automatically\n   and drop the result.\n3. If the standing is `frozen`, federation staff must decide whether to leave\n   the frozen table in place during review or deliberately unfreeze or\n   force-recompute it after governance review.\n4. If the standing is public (`website_published = True`) and the table should\n   be withdrawn during review, unpublish it separately. Publication is not a\n   standings state.\n5. A governance override request may document the review, but it does not keep\n   a contested result official.\n\n## Contested Results and the Frozen Table\n\n| Standing status | Operator action |\n|----------------|-----------------|\n| `draft` / `computed` | Automatic recompute removes the contested result |\n| `frozen` | Federation manager decides whether to unfreeze or force-recompute after review |\n| `website_published = True` | Unpublish separately if the public table should be hidden during review |\n\n## Summary of Access Control\n\n| Action | Required Group |\n|--------|---------------|\n| Manual recompute | `group_federation_manager` |\n| Freeze standings | `group_federation_manager` |\n| Publish / unpublish | `group_federation_manager` |\n| View standings | `group_federation_user` (backend), public (website) |\n\n## Related Workflows\n\n- [WORKFLOW_RESULT_PIPELINE.md](WORKFLOW_RESULT_PIPELINE.md) — Result approval that triggers automatic recompute.\n- [WORKFLOW_APPEAL_DISPUTE.md](WORKFLOW_APPEAL_DISPUTE.md) — Appeal and dispute process for contested results.\n- [WORKFLOW_PUBLIC_PUBLICATION.md](WORKFLOW_PUBLIC_PUBLICATION.md) — Broader public-site publication workflow.\n", "content_length": 6867, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "_workflows/WORKFLOW_STANDINGS_LIFECYCLE.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "5f4f4090720ce7beaeb793767efd8dae49614b26c3b90434ad07c34f150aa2f3", "size_bytes": 6889}
-{"content": "# Workflow: Tournament Lifecycle\n\nFull lifecycle of a tournament — from competition definition and participant\nenrolment through schedule generation, match execution, and final completion.\n\n## Overview\n\nA **competition** is a recurring series (e.g. \"National League Division 1\").\nWithin each season, competitions host one or more **tournaments** which are\nstructured into stages, groups, and matches. This workflow covers the entire\njourney from initial setup to final completion.\n\nCanonical readiness chain (registration to publication):\n\n1. Confirm season registration.\n2. Confirm tournament participant.\n3. Prepare active ready roster and match-day sheets.\n4. Publish schedule and run live operations.\n5. Approve results.\n6. Recompute/review standings.\n7. Publish tournament and standings surfaces.\n\nBlocking vs warning-only model:\n\n- Blocking: the step cannot proceed (for example, deadline-backed roster blockers\n   or unresolved publication validation blockers).\n- Warning-only: the step can proceed, but requires operator follow-up and may\n   require manager override logging depending on the surface.\n\n## Modules Involved\n\n| Module | Role |\n|--------|------|\n| `sports_federation_base` | Seasons, clubs, teams |\n| `sports_federation_rules` | Rule sets governing scoring, tie-breaks, eligibility |\n| `sports_federation_tournament` | Competition, tournament, stage, group, participant, match models |\n| `sports_federation_competition_core`, `sports_federation_registration` | Competition identity, lifecycle, registration, and participant finalization |\n| `sports_federation_format` | Versioned logical structures and stage graphs |\n| `sports_federation_calendar` | Physical match days, capacity, slots, and timelines |\n| `sports_federation_scheduling` | Deterministic fixture assignment and schedule validation |\n| `sports_federation_schedule_approval` | Schedule review and immutable publication snapshots |\n| `sports_federation_matchday` | Live operations after schedule publication |\n| `sports_federation_venues` | Venue and playing-area assignment |\n| `sports_federation_standings` | Standings computation at each stage |\n| `sports_federation_notifications` | Participant-confirmation and publication notifications |\n| `sports_federation_public_site` | Public publication of tournament pages |\n\n## Verified UI navigation\n\nUse [`docs/COMPETITION_UI_WORKFLOW.md`](../docs/COMPETITION_UI_WORKFLOW.md). The main journey is under **Federation → Competition Workflow**; addon names below describe ownership, not menu labels.\n\n## Step-by-Step Flow\n\n### 1. Competition Setup\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_rules`, `sports_federation_tournament`\n\n1. Define a **rule set** with scoring values (win/draw/loss points), tie-break\n   criteria, squad-size limits, and eligibility rules.\n2. Create a **competition** (e.g. \"National League Division 1\").\n3. Link the competition to the active season and the rule set.\n4. Set competition state to `active`.\n\n### 2. Tournament Creation\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_tournament`\n\n1. Under the competition, create a **tournament** (e.g. \"NL Div 1 — Season 2025\").\n2. Set tournament type: `league`, `cup`, `friendly`, or `playoff`.\n3. Assign date range, rule set (inherited from competition or overridden).\n4. Set maximum participants if applicable.\n5. If the competition is spread over multiple event days, plan the shared\n   schedule blocks directly on the stage rounds. Each round can carry a\n   calendar date and a venue, while the matches inside that round keep their\n   own kickoff times.\n6. Tournament starts in `draft` state.\n\n### 3. Venue Assignment\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_venues`\n\n1. Create or select venues with address, capacity, and playing areas.\n2. Link venues to the tournament via the `venues` Many2many field.\n3. Individual matches can later reference specific venues and playing areas.\n\n### 4. Participant Enrolment\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator (or via import)\n**Module**: `sports_federation_tournament`, `sports_federation_import_tools`\n\n1. Add **participants** to the tournament — each links a team to the tournament.\n    - If the flow starts from portal registration requests, an administrator first\n       confirms the `federation.competition.entry` record. That creates or links\n       a `federation.tournament.participant` record in state `registered`.\n    - That participant must still be moved to state `confirmed` before schedule\n       generation can use it.\n2. Optionally assign participants to specific stages and groups.\n3. Set seeding ranks for bracket placement.\n4. Participant states: `registered` → `confirmed` → `withdrawn` / `eliminated`.\n5. Participant confirmation can happen before the team has an active roster, but\n   only until one week before its first scheduled match, or one week before\n   tournament start if no match has been scheduled yet. Once that deadline is\n   reached, participant confirmation is blocked until the team has an active\n   ready roster. When both a competition-specific roster and a season-wide\n   roster are available, the competition-specific roster is used for readiness\n   checks.\n6. The participant form now surfaces the current roster deadline feedback inline\n   and exposes **Open Team Roster** when operators need to resolve the blocker\n   in the rosters flow before confirmation can continue.\n7. Confirming a participant sends an email to the team and club contacts.\n8. Move tournament to `open` state once enrolment is complete.\n\nBulk enrolment is available via the **Import Tournament Participants** wizard.\n\n### 5. Stage & Group Structure\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_tournament`\n\n1. Create **stages** within the tournament (e.g. \"Group Phase\", \"Quarter-Finals\").\n2. Set stage type: `group`, `knockout`, `playoff`, or `other`.\n3. Order stages by sequence.\n4. Within each stage, create **groups** (e.g. \"Group A\", \"Pool 1\").\n5. Assign participants to groups.\n6. Create or review the stage rounds that should exist for each phase. Example:\n   rounds 1-4 for the round-robin stage, then knockout rounds on the final stage.\n\n### 6. Schedule Generation\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Modules**: `sports_federation_format`, `sports_federation_calendar`,\n`sports_federation_scheduling`, `sports_federation_schedule_approval`, and\n`sports_federation_matchday`\n\nThe path is an explicit sequence of handovers:\n\n- Freeze the logical structure and stage graph in `sports_federation_format`.\n- Prepare physical match days and playable capacity in\n   `sports_federation_calendar`.\n- Generate or assign fixtures and validate the complete draft in\n   `sports_federation_scheduling`.\n- Submit the draft for review and publish an immutable snapshot through\n   `sports_federation_schedule_approval`.\n- Start live operations only from the published snapshot through\n   `sports_federation_matchday`.\n\n1. Move the competition into the state that permits scheduling.\n2. Registration finalizes and locks the confirmed participant set.\n3. Format freezes the structure and stage graph for the competition edition.\n   Round-robin and knockout generation remain deterministic and scoped to the\n   frozen structure.\n4. Calendar creates match days and `federation.schedule.slot` capacity for the\n   required venues and courts. Slot lifecycle and court timelines are owned by\n   `sports_federation_calendar`.\n5. Scheduling assigns fixtures to available slots, applies fairness and rest\n   validation, and returns a complete draft schedule. Blocking conflicts must be\n   resolved before review; warnings remain visible and auditable.\n6. Schedule approval reviews the draft and publishes an immutable schedule\n   snapshot. Federation managers may approve configured warning-only overrides,\n   with the reason retained in the audit trail.\n7. Match-day operations open and close only published schedules. Referee\n   readiness, venue readiness, result follow-up, and incidents are handled by\n   their owning modules without changing the approved snapshot.\n\n**Round Robin**: The format service generates a complete deterministic pairing\nset where every team plays every other team once or twice according to policy.\n\n**Knockout**: The format service creates a seeded single-elimination bracket,\nincluding byes and future-round wiring for non-power-of-two participant counts.\n\n### 7. Match Execution\n\n**Actor**: Federation staff, referees\n**Module**: `sports_federation_tournament`\n\n1. Matches are scheduled with date/time, venue, home/away teams.\n2. Match states progress: `draft` → `scheduled` → `in_progress` → `done`.\n3. Scores are entered on the match form (home_score, away_score).\n4. Match-day details are handled by the [Match Day Operations](WORKFLOW_MATCH_DAY_OPERATIONS.md)\n   workflow.\n\n### 8. Standings Computation\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_standings`\n\n1. Create a **standings** record scoped to the tournament, stage, or group.\n2. Link the rule set for scoring and tie-break rules.\n3. Compute standings: aggregates match results into ranked lines.\n4. States: `draft` → `computed` → `frozen`.\n5. Frozen standings are the publication candidates for the public site.\n\n### 9. Stage Progression\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_tournament`\n\n1. After a stage completes, review standings to determine qualifiers.\n2. Qualification rules from the rule set indicate who advances.\n3. Use `federation.stage.progression` rules to formalise advancement: these\n   can be single-group, cross-group (e.g. \"best third-placed teams\"), and\n   include seeding/placement strategies. A progression rule can be executed\n   manually (`action_execute()`) or set to `auto_advance=True`.\n    - When designing a versioned structure in Format Studio, use the\n       structure-scoped `federation.structure.stage.progression` edges instead.\n       These graph edges are separate from the competition engine's tournament\n       progression rules and are validated before the structure is generated.\n   - When a standings record is `frozen`/`computed`, any progression rules for\n     that stage with `auto_advance=True` will be executed automatically — new\n     participants are created in the target stage and (optionally) a new stage\n     schedule can be generated automatically.\n4. Tournament templates (`federation.tournament.template`) let administrators\n   scaffold common stage/group/progression combinations (for recurring\n   tournaments). Use `action_apply()` from the template to create stages and\n   progression rules for a tournament in a single step.\n5. Generate the next stage in **Federation → Competition Workflow → Format Studio**, then assign it in **Schedule Planner**.\n6. Typical workflow: freeze the round-robin standing, auto-advance the top-ranked\n   teams into the knockout stage through a `federation.stage.progression` rule,\n   then schedule those knockout matches onto the planned knockout rounds.\n\n### 10. Tournament Completion\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_tournament`\n\n1. After the final stage, review and approve all remaining results.\n2. Compute and publish final standings.\n3. Set tournament state to `closed`.\n4. Competition can be closed at end of season.\n\n### 11. Public Publication\n\n**Actor**: Federation administrator\n**Module**: `sports_federation_public_site`\n\n1. Set `website_published = True` on the tournament.\n2. Configure public slug, description, and toggle results/standings visibility.\n   The tournament Website tab now states whether publication is blocked because\n   the tournament is still unpublished, standings do not exist yet, or standings\n   remain hidden, and it links back to the standings action when relevant.\n3. Publish standings records. Standings forms also explain whether approved\n   results are still pending or whether website publication is the next valid\n   step.\n4. Participant club and team contacts receive a tournament-publication email the first time the tournament is published.\n5. Public pages become available at `/competitions/<edition-slug>` and the related\n   canonical `/competitions/...` route family.\n\n## State Diagram\n\n```\nCompetition: draft → active → closed\n\nTournament: draft → open → in_progress → closed\n                                       → cancelled\n\nMatch: draft → scheduled → in_progress → done\n                                        → cancelled\n\nStandings: draft → computed → frozen\n\nParticipant: registered → confirmed → withdrawn\n                                    → eliminated\n```\n\n## Key Decision Points\n\n| Question | Outcome |\n|----------|---------|\n| League or Cup format? | Determines round-robin vs. knockout wizard |\n| How many stages? | Single-stage league or multi-stage tournament with progression |\n| Power-of-two bracket? | Knockout wizard handles byes for odd counts |\n| When to publish? | Standings should be computed and verified before publication |\n\n## Related Workflows\n\n- [Match Day Operations](WORKFLOW_MATCH_DAY_OPERATIONS.md) — detailed match-day process\n- [Result Pipeline](WORKFLOW_RESULT_PIPELINE.md) — score verification and approval\n- [Season Registration](WORKFLOW_SEASON_REGISTRATION.md) — prerequisite club/team registration\n", "content_length": 13307, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "_workflows/WORKFLOW_TOURNAMENT_LIFECYCLE.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "11d7ca4871c052911bf5c52d833dbc3299f598440aa57e75114da763d970048b", "size_bytes": 13371}

 {"content": "# ADR-0001: Portal Trust Boundaries\n\nLast updated: 2026-08-20\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-08-20\nReview cadence: Every release\nStatus: Accepted\n\n## Context\n\nPortal club representatives and officials must create or update federation records without receiving broad backend ACLs. Controller-only checks are insufficient because direct model calls, guessed identifiers, or future routes could otherwise widen access.\n\n## Decision\n\nPortal writes use explicit, model-owned privilege boundaries:\n\n- Controllers resolve the request user and the candidate record, reject malformed input, and invoke a model-owned portal method.\n- Ownership and scope are enforced again in the model or shared privilege service.\n- Elevated reads and writes go through `federation.portal.privilege`, including helpers such as `elevate()`, `portal_search()`, `portal_create()`, `portal_write()`, and `portal_call()` where applicable.\n- The privilege boundary preserves the request user for audit attribution while keeping elevation narrow and explicit.\n- Controllers must not perform business writes through raw `sudo()`.\n- Positive in-scope, negative out-of-scope, direct-ID, and elevated-helper tests are mandatory for every privileged portal write surface.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Privilege escalation remains centralized and reviewable.\n- Controller and ORM boundaries fail closed independently.\n- Cross-club and team-scoped access can be regression-tested consistently.\n- New portal features must reuse the privilege service or add a reviewed model-owned equivalent.\n- Raw elevated controller writes are treated as security defects.\n", "content_length": 1629, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "adr/0001-portal-trust-boundaries.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "2c05056fbddc6d0400083a690deca702e9800c026de6e87185e537ebea6576fe", "size_bytes": 1629}
 {"content": "# ADR-0002: Reporting SQL Views\n\nLast updated: 2026-04-18\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-08-20\nReview cadence: Every release\nStatus: Accepted\n\n## Context\n\nFederation reporting combines finance, standings, compliance, notification, planning, and workflow data across multiple addons. Rebuilding those joins in controllers or repeated ORM loops would duplicate logic and create unpredictable performance.\n\n## Decision\n\nOperational and planning projections remain read-only analytical models backed by PostgreSQL views when their data is naturally cross-module or aggregation-heavy.\n\n- SQL-backed report models use `_auto = False`.\n- View definitions are recreated deterministically from `init()` or the repository's approved view helper.\n- Controllers and exports consume report models instead of embedding substantial SQL or cross-module aggregation logic.\n- Report models are read-only and must not masquerade as writable business records.\n- Heavy reports retain query budgets, representative fixtures, and performance watchpoints.\n- SQL view changes are upgrade-sensitive and require migration review evidence.\n- A normal stored Odoo model is preferred when the data has its own lifecycle or must be edited.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Cross-module reporting logic remains centralized.\n- Export and operator surfaces share the same projection semantics.\n- View dependencies and upgrade order require explicit review.\n- Maintainers must preserve query plans, migration safety, and read-only behavior.\n", "content_length": 1514, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "adr/0002-reporting-sql-views.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "ef36c1653fd664b1b66d727fab316472e1dd05aad0b7e71a28d0f01cd5a889ad", "size_bytes": 1514}

Create the season competition\n\nPreferred menu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Create Competition\n```\n\nThe wizard selects the setup template, competition template, season, dates, optional rule set, registration dates, divisions, and responsibilities. It creates the season competition, divisions, registration windows, and role assignments, then opens the season competition.\n\nInspect the records through:\n\n```text\nFederation > Setup > Competition Setup > Season Competitions\nFederation > Planning > Advanced Records > Divisions & Tournaments\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Competition Overview\n```\n\n**Recovery:** Correct newly created records before clubs submit. There is no generic **Undo Competition Wizard** button. If downstream entries, fixtures, schedules, results, or publications exist, preserve the original records and create controlled replacements.\n\n### 3. Open registration and accept entries\n\nBackend:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Registration Desk\n```\n\nClub portal:\n\n```text\nMy Account > Season registrations\n```\n\nUse **Open Registration** on a draft registration window. Clubs prepare and submit entries. Managers review them in the Registration Desk.\n\n**Recovery:** Use **Close Registration** to stop submissions. A submitted entry can be withdrawn by the club or returned by the manager with a reason. A returned entry can be corrected and resubmitted. Rejection remains historical evidence.\n\n### 4. Finalize participants\n\nMenu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Registration Desk\n```\n\nClose the registration window and press **Finalize Participants**. The finalized participant set feeds the format structure.\n\n**Recovery:** Correct entries before finalization. If a finalized set is wrong and nothing depends on it, create a corrected set through the registration workflow. If fixtures or schedules exist, create a successor structure or schedule revision instead of mutating published history.\n\n### 5. Configure and generate the format\n\nMenus:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Format Templates\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Format Studio\n```\n\n**Format Templates** is manager-only. In **Format Studio**, select the season competition, division, finalized participant set, and format settings. Use **Check Feasibility**, then **Generate Fixtures**. For multi-stage structures use **Validate Stage Graph**. Once accepted, use **Freeze Structure**.\n\n**Recovery:** Before freeze, correct and regenerate. Once operational matches or frozen stage snapshots exist, create a new structure version. The current UI has no generic structure-unfreeze command.\n\n### 6. Prepare and progress stages\n\nThere is no standalone **Stage Progression** menu. Stage controls are on the structure opened from:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Format Studio\n```\n\nAvailable stage actions are **Prepare**, **Start**, and **Freeze & Progress**.\n\n**Recovery:** Correct a stage before starting it. Before progression, correct and recompute standings. Frozen snapshot lines are immutable; after progression use a corrected successor structure rather than editing evidence.\n\n### 7. Plan calendar capacity\n\nMenu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Calendar Planner\n```\n\nCreate match days, slot windows, and capacity, then use **Mark Capacity Ready**. Venue setup and constraints are under:\n\n```text\nFederation > Match Day > Venues\n```\n\n**Recovery:** Edit draft calendar records. If a schedule already uses the calendar, make the deliberate calendar correction and refresh the working schedule. Stale assignments are flagged, not silently deleted.\n\n### 8. Build the working schedule\n\nMenu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Schedule Planner\n```\n\nUse **Refresh Calendar Fixtures**. Assign dates, times, venues, and courts manually, or use **Auto-schedule**, **Preview**, and **Apply Auto-schedule**. Review fairness warnings.\n\n**Recovery:** Draft and change-requested schedules remain editable. A preview does not change the schedule until applied. Refresh fixtures, move assignments, or regenerate while mutable.\n\n### 9. Submit and review the schedule\n\nPlanner menu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Schedule Planner\n```\n\nUse **Submit for Review**. Approver menu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Schedule Review Queue\n```\n\nThe review exposes **Withdraw Submission**, **Request Changes**, and **Approve Schedule** according to state and role.\n\n**Recovery:** Withdraw a pending submission to return it to editing. +{"content": "# Federation Backend Navigation\n\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast verified against menu XML: 2026-09-04\nReview cadence: Every release\n\n## Goal\n\nThe Federation backend is organized around operator intent, not addon names or implementation layers. A user should be able to decide where to go from the business task they are performing. The root navigation therefore has seven stable work areas:\n\n1. **Competitions**: define, create, register, structure, schedule, and review competitions.\n2. **Clubs & People**: maintain clubs, teams, players, licenses, representatives, and season registrations.\n3. **Match Operations**: run match days and manage fixtures, match sheets, venues, officials, and discipline.\n4. **Publishing**: expose approved schedules, standings, and editorial content.\n5. **Finance & Assurance**: manage finance, compliance, and governed exceptions.\n6. **Insights**: review readiness, performance, assurance signals, trends, and scheduled reports.\n7. **Administration**: process operational tasks, integrations, notifications, retention, and technical job health.\n\n## Design rules\n\n- Root tabs represent durable business responsibilities. They must not mirror addon names.\n- A record has one primary navigation home. Cross-links on forms may provide shortcuts, but duplicate root entries are avoided.\n- Daily workflow entries precede configuration and technical records.\n- Technical and audit records remain available, but are grouped at the end of their owning area.\n- Manager-only items stay role-gated. Reparenting a menu must not broaden its groups or model access.\n- Empty compatibility categories are not retained. Existing XML IDs are reused where practical so upgrades move menus instead of creating duplicates.\n- New menus must fit one of the seven work areas. Adding another root tab requires an update to this document and the navigation contract check.\n\n## Intended menu map\n\n```text\nFederation\n├── Competitions\n│   ├── Seasons\n│   ├── Season Competitions\n│   ├── Competition Operations\n│   │   ├── Create Competition\n│   │   ├── Competition Overview\n│   │   ├── Registration Desk\n│   │   ├── Format Studio\n│   │   ├── Calendar Planner\n│   │   ├── Schedule Planner\n│   │   ├── Schedule Review Queue\n│   │   └── Audit & Technical Records\n│   ├── Competition Templates\n│   ├── Format Templates\n│   ├── Rules & Policies\n│   └── Competition Records\n├── Clubs & People\n│   ├── Club Directory\n│   ├── Players & Licensing\n│   ├── Representatives & Access\n│   └── Season Registrations\n├── Match Operations\n│   ├── Match-Day Control\n│   ├── Matches\n│   ├── Match Sheets\n│   ├── Officiating\n│   ├── Venues\n│   └── Discipline\n├── Publishing\n│   ├── Approved Schedules\n│   ├── Schedule Publications\n│   ├── Standings\n│   └── Public Editorial\n├── Finance & Assurance\n│   ├── Finance\n│   ├── Compliance\n│   └── Governance\n├── Insights\n│   └── Reports & Insights\n│       ├── Overview & Readiness\n│       ├── Performance\n│       ├── Assurance & Exceptions\n│       └── Automation & History\n└── Administration\n    ├── Action Queue\n    ├── Notification Centre\n    ├── Imports & Integrations\n    └── System Health\n```\n\nMenus hidden by security groups are omitted for users who do not own that responsibility.  {"content": "# Competition Workflow Ownership\n\nThe ownership chain is the supported competition-planning architecture. No\nproduction data migration is required solely for this ownership clarification.\n\n## Capability ownership\n\n- Competition Core owns edition lifecycle and role assignments.\n- Registration owns entries and versioned finalized participant sets.\n- Format Studio owns stage topology, logical fixtures, standings snapshots, and progression.\n- Calendar owns physical match days, courts, and availability slots.\n- Scheduling owns fixture-to-slot assignments and fairness proposals.\n- Schedule Approval owns independent review and immutable publications.\n- Result Control owns the complete result lifecycle.\n- Match-Day Operations owns live execution and incidents.\n\n## Domain event contract\n\nEvents are past-tense facts. Producers emit only after a successful state change. Consumers must be idempotent and may not mutate the producer aggregate. Event payloads contain stable record IDs, version/revision, actor, and reason where applicable.\n\nRequired events: participant_set_finalized, structure_frozen, stage_standings_frozen, stage_progression_applied, matchday_capacity_ready, schedule_submitted, schedule_approved, schedule_published, matchday_opened, result_approved, result_contested, result_corrected, matchday_closed.\n", "content_length": 1325, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "docs/competition_engine_ownership.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "3352ecae7e79ab9a7fa5079eca2e62c212b65a59136effde4e6945b21563894c", "size_bytes": 1325}

 {"content": "# Human Acceptance Test for Release Candidate\n\n## 1. Purpose\n\nValidate the complete federation workflow with realistic roles, data, devices, and recovery scenarios before tagging RC1.\n\n## 2. Participants\n\nAssign separate people where practical:\n\n- Release coordinator\n- Federation administrator\n- Tournament manager\n- Club representative A\n- Club representative B from another club\n- Referee or officiating coordinator\n- Result validator\n- Result approver\n- Observer taking notes and evidence\n\n## 3. Preparation\n\n1. Deploy the exact candidate commit to a disposable production-like environment.\n2. Restore an anonymized recent database or create representative test data.\n3. Configure outbound email to a safe test inbox.\n4. Enable the same reverse proxy, workers, timeout, attachment, and database settings planned for production.\n5. Create two clubs, at least eight teams, twelve players per team, four courts, two gamedays, and user accounts for every role.\n6. Record the commit SHA, database snapshot identifier, browser versions, start time, and participants.\n7. Confirm a restore point exists before testing.\n8. Open a defect log with severity, reproduction steps, evidence, owner, and disposition columns.\n\n## 4. Entry criteria\n\n- RC CI workflow is green.\n- Database upgrade completed without unresolved warnings.\n- No critical or high defect is open.\n- Test users can sign in and their role memberships are verified.\n- Email delivery and system time are correct.\n\n## 5. Test sequence\n\n### A. Competition and rules setup\n\n1. Administrator creates a season, competition edition, rule set, and division.\n2. Configure scoring, tie-breaks, squad limits, qualification, and required officials.\n3. Lock the rule set.\n4. Attempt to change locked scoring values. Expected: change is blocked.\n5. Duplicate the rules for a future version. Expected: historical configuration remains unchanged.\n6. Open the tournament. Expected: competition identity and effective rules can no longer change silently.\n\n### B. Club portal isolation\n\n1. Club A representative signs in on desktop.\n2. Create or update Club A teams, contacts, registration, and roster.\n3. Club B representative performs the same actions for Club B.\n4. Manually substitute a Club B record ID in a Club A URL or request.\n5. Expected: access is denied without revealing Club B data.\n6. Repeat one registration and roster workflow on a mobile viewport.\n7. Sign out, expire a session, and retry a pending action. Expected: safe recovery without duplicate submission.\n\n### C. Stage and progression builder\n\n1. Manager creates a group phase followed by knockout and placement stages.\n2. Create groups, rounds, and progression mappings.\n3. Attempt a self-referencing or cyclic progression. Expected: blocked.\n4. Preview deletion of an unused stage. Expected: dependencies are listed accurately.\n5. Attempt deletion of a stage with matches. Expected: explicit warning or block according to policy.\n6. Confirm rollback leaves the original structure intact when deletion is cancelled.\n\n### D. Gamedays and schedule planning\n\n1. Create one shared gameday for two divisions.\n2. Generate slots across four courts with a planned break.\n3. Assign fixed matches manually.\n4. Run auto-schedule preview and compare warnings with the planner.\n5. Execute scheduling and inspect rest time, court conflicts, duplicate matches, and unscheduled matches.\n6. Open the planner as a second manager.\n7. Manager A moves a match. Manager B submits an action from the stale screen.\n8. Expected: Manager B receives a clear stale-revision conflict and Manager A's change remains.\n9. Test undo and redo after a normal assignment.\n10. Attempt to assign two matches to the same slot. Expected: one assignment only.\n\n### E. Validation and publication\n\n1. Validate the completed gameday.\n2. Change one assignment after validation.\n3. Attempt publication. Expected: rejected because validation is stale.\n4. Validate again and publish.\n5. Confirm the published schedule is visible to the correct portal users.\n6. Republish with an override reason where policy permits warnings.\n7. Confirm hard blockers cannot be bypassed by a reason.\n\n### F. Officiating\n\n1. Assign a qualified referee and confirm the duty.\n2. Attempt to complete an unconfirmed assignment. Expected: blocked.\n3. Create an overlapping assignment. Expected: conflict or explicit warning according to policy.\n4. Confirm the portal user can see only their own duty.\n5. Complete the confirmed duty and verify timestamps and audit history.\n\n### G. Results and standings\n\n1. Enter results through the intended portal or operator workflow.\n2. Submit, verify, and approve with three distinct users.\n3. Expected: submitter cannot verify or approve their own result.\n4. Confirm approved results appear in official standings.\n5. Attempt direct reset of an approved result. Expected: blocked.\n6. Contest and correct the result through the audited workflow.\n7. Reapprove and verify standings and knockout progression recalculate correctly.\n\n### H. Notifications and operational queues\n\n1. Trigger registration, publication, referee, and result notifications.\n2. Confirm recipients, language, links, and duplicate prevention.\n3. Simulate a recoverable delivery failure.\n4. Acknowledge and retry it through the operator workflow.\n5. Confirm the operational queue exposes actionable failures without leaking sensitive information.\n\n### I. Recovery and resilience\n\n1. Take a database backup after publication.\n2. Perform a controlled application restart during a non-destructive workflow.\n3. Confirm users recover without duplicate writes.\n4. Restore the backup to a separate environment.\n5. Verify competition, schedule, assignments, results, audits, and attachments.\n6. Execute the documented rollback procedure for the candidate build.\n\n## 6. Evidence to collect\n\n- Screenshots of each major workflow and expected block\n- CI run URL and commit SHA\n- Database migration and restore logs\n- Email samples with personal data removed\n- Conflict and access-denied responses\n- Final standings and bracket export\n- Defect log with disposition\n- Signed approval record\n\n## 7. Severity and exit criteria\n\n- **Critical**: data loss, privilege escape, incorrect official outcome, unrecoverable deployment. RC is blocked.\n- **High**: core workflow unavailable, duplicate schedule, broken progression, migration failure. RC is blocked.\n- **Medium**: workaround exists but materially harms operations. Release owner decides with documented acceptance.\n- **Low**: cosmetic or minor usability issue. May be deferred.\n\nPass only when all mandatory scenarios are completed, no critical or high defects remain, restore and rollback succeed, and every required approver signs the release ticket.\n", "content_length": 6743, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "docs/release/HUMAN_ACCEPTANCE_TEST.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "78a37e92ec260a1e20dec57f1ea1bfc9704ea3e2c8c49510447a85e6da49ffa8", "size_bytes": 6743}

The wizard requests:\n\n- the active venue playing areas to use;\n- the local game-day start and end time;\n- one total slot duration per match;\n- whether a noon pause begins at 12:00 and its duration;\n- whether an existing slot plan may be replaced.\n\nThe total slot duration is the complete playing-area occupancy and must include normal play, possible overtime, post-match clearance, and setup for the next match. There is no separate hidden buffer that could make the published times misleading.\n\nThe preview reports playable slots, explicit noon-break rows, and candidates rejected by active venue or playing-area constraint windows. Start, end, and pause times are interpreted in the user timezone and stored as the corresponding UTC instants. Generation preserves those planned times when it creates the rows, including explicit break rows; it does not rebase generated rows onto a playing area's existing timeline. Generation creates only slots that finish inside the requested game-day window. Venue-wide constraints affect every selected playing area; area-specific constraints affect only that area.  {"content": "Sports Federation Compliance\n============================\n\nDocument requirements, submissions, and compliance checking. Ensures that\nclubs, players, referees, and venues maintain all required documentation\n(licenses, insurance certificates, safety reports, and similar evidence).\n\nPurpose\n-------\n\nDefines what **documents are required** for each entity type, tracks\n**submissions** with attachments and expiry dates, and runs\n**compliance checks** to flag missing or expired documentation.\n\nDependencies\n------------\n\n- ``sports_federation_base``: Clubs.\n- ``sports_federation_people``: Players.\n- ``sports_federation_officiating``: Referees.\n- ``sports_federation_venues``: Venues.\n- ``sports_federation_portal``: Club representatives.\n- ``mail``: Chatter.\n\nModels\n------\n\n``federation.document.requirement``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nA type of document that certain entities must provide.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``name`` (Char): Requirement title.\n- ``code`` (Char): Unique code.\n- ``target_model`` (Selection): Entity type such as club, player, referee,\n   venue, or club representative.\n- ``required_for_all`` (Boolean): Applies to all entities of that type.\n- ``requires_expiry_date`` (Boolean): Submission must include an expiry date.\n- ``validity_days`` (Integer): Default validity period.\n- ``description`` (Text): Detailed requirements.\n- ``active`` (Boolean): Whether the requirement is currently enforced.\n\n``federation.document.submission``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nAn actual document submitted against a requirement.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``name`` (Char): Submission title.\n- ``requirement_id`` (Many2one): Requirement being fulfilled.\n- ``target_model`` (Selection, computed): Copied from the requirement.\n- ``club_id`` / ``player_id`` / ``referee_id`` / ``venue_id`` /\n   ``club_representative_id`` (Many2one): Target entity.\n- ``status`` (Selection): ``draft``, ``submitted``, ``approved``,\n   ``rejected``, ``replacement_requested``, or ``expired``.\n- ``attachment_ids`` (Many2many): Uploaded files.\n- ``issue_date`` / ``expiry_date`` (Date): Document validity.\n- ``reviewer_id`` (Many2one): Reviewer.\n- ``reviewed_on`` (Datetime): Review timestamp.\n- ``is_expired`` (Boolean, computed): True when ``expiry_date`` is before\n   today.\n- ``target_display`` (Char, computed): Readable target entity name.\n- ``notes`` (Text): Remarks.\n\n- **State machine**: ``draft -> submitted -> approved / rejected /\n   replacement_requested -> expired``.\n- **Constraint**: exactly one target entity field must be set.\n- **Expired ribbon**: shown in the form view when the document has passed its\n   expiry date.\n\n``federation.compliance.check``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nA check result linking a requirement to an entity's submission status.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``name`` (Char): Check title.\n- ``target_model`` (Selection): Entity type.\n- ``club_id`` / ``player_id`` / ``referee_id`` / ``venue_id`` /\n   ``club_representative_id`` (Many2one): Target.\n- ``status`` (Selection): ``compliant``, ``missing``, ``pending``, or\n   ``expired``.\n- ``requirement_id`` (Many2one): Requirement being checked.\n- ``submission_id`` (Many2one): Linked submission, when available.\n- ``checked_on`` (Datetime): Check timestamp.\n- ``note`` (Char): Result note.\n- ``target_display`` (Char, computed): Readable target name.\n\n``federation.compliance.check.archive``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nImmutable history row capturing how a compliance check looked at a point in\ntime.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``compliance_check_id`` (Many2one): Source compliance check.\n- ``archived_on`` / ``checked_on`` (Datetime): Archive timestamp and source\n   check timestamp.\n- ``target_model`` / ``target_res_id`` (Char / Integer): Archived target\n   reference.\n- ``requirement_id`` / ``submission_id`` (Many2one): Requirement and linked\n   submission snapshot.\n- ``status`` (Selection): Archived compliance status.\n- ``note`` (Char): Archived operator note.\n\nKey Behaviours\n--------------\n\n- **Requirement definition**: federation staff define which documents each\n   entity type must provide.\n- **Submission workflow**: documents are uploaded, submitted, and reviewed with\n   approval or rejection outcomes.\n- **Expiry tracking**: computed ``is_expired`` flags overdue documents.\n- **Compliance checks**: programmatic checks produce compliant, missing,\n   pending, or expired statuses per entity.\n- **Multi-entity support**: the same framework covers clubs, players,\n   referees, venues, and club representatives.\n- **Portal self-service workspace**: scoped portal users can review their own\n   requirements, renewal deadlines, remediation notes, and submission history\n   at ``/my/compliance``.\n- **Portal submission flow**: club representatives and referees can upload\n   replacement documents and submit renewals directly from the portal detail\n   page without backend access. The controller delegates the write to\n   ``federation.document.submission._portal_submit_submission()`` so\n   attachment creation and submission state changes stay inside the model\n   boundary.\n- **Historical evidence**: compliance checks append archive rows on create and\n   on tracked status changes so operators can review how a target moved from\n   missing to compliant over time.\n\nPortal Self-Service\n-------------------\n\nPortal routes:\n\n- ``GET /my/compliance``: workspace listing with renewal warnings, review\n   state, and attention-first sorting.\n- ``GET /my/compliance/<requirement_id>/<target_model>/<target_id>``: detail\n   page for one requirement and target record.\n- ``POST /my/compliance/<requirement_id>/<target_model>/<target_id>/submit``:\n   attachment-backed submission or renewal request.\n\nPortal workspace behaviour:\n\n- Access is limited to targets the current portal user is allowed to manage.\n- Remediation notes from the reporting layer are surfaced when available.\n- Renewal windows are highlighted before expiry so replacement documents can be\n   submitted proactively.\n- Attachment creation preserves portal user identity while still using\n   controlled elevated writes through\n   ``_portal_submit_submission()`` and\n   ``_portal_create_submission_attachments()``.\n", "content_length": 6137, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_compliance/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "4817eb140f800f12ca9c5daf68004c3a269979bfb866470a7377d350c0a100c4", "size_bytes": 6137}

Install the module with demo data enabled in Odoo.\n2. Open core workflows from tournament setup through match completion.\n3. Reset by recreating the database when you need a fresh deterministic dataset.\n\nScope and constraints\n- This module is for non-production environments.\n- Demo records prioritize workflow coverage over real-world data volume.\n- The seeded Spring Cup intentionally omits category and gender restrictions\n  because its participant fixture demonstrates senior, youth, and women's\n  teams in one navigable competition.\n- Data is versioned with the addon and intended to stay reproducible across installs.\n\nValidation checklist\n- Module installs without additional manual data steps.\n- Tournament, roster, and standings flows are navigable from seeded records.\n- Portal/public pages can render at least one realistic competition storyline.\n\n## Release-pilot qualification\n\nThe integrated P0-P3 release path is documented in\n`docs/RELEASE_PILOT_SCENARIO.md`. Run\n`scripts/ci/run_rc_validation.sh focus` before promoting a release candidate.\n\n## Accessible operator training walkthrough\n\nUse the deterministic demo database with a federation manager who also has the\ncompetition administrator, registration manager, competition designer, calendar\nplanner, schedule planner, schedule approver, and match-day manager roles.\n\nComplete the normal path without a mouse:\n\n1. Open **Competition Overview** and move through controls with `Tab` and\n   `Shift+Tab`. The focused control must always have a visible outline.\n2. Continue through **Registration**, **Format**, **Calendar**, **Schedule**, and\n   **Review**, activating links and buttons with `Enter` or `Space`.\n3. Submit an incomplete portal form. Focus must move to the error summary, and\n   invalid controls must reference that summary through `aria-describedby`.\n4. Open and close a confirmation modal. Focus must enter the modal and return to\n   the control that opened it.\n5. Repeat the club portal's competition, roster, officiating, and result tasks at\n   a 390 CSS-pixel viewport. No primary action may require horizontal page\n   scrolling.\n6. Confirm that every state is expressed as readable text. Color and icons may\n   reinforce the state but must not be the only status signal.\n\nThe `keyboard_competition_setup` browser tour qualifies the canonical backend\njourney mechanically. Portal template accessibility and mobile tests qualify\nlabels, error semantics, status text, responsive tables, and action wrapping.\n\n\n## Verified operator menu guide\n\nUse [`docs/COMPETITION_UI_WORKFLOW.md`](../docs/COMPETITION_UI_WORKFLOW.md) during training and acceptance. Install the module with demo data enabled in Odoo.\n2. Open core workflows from tournament setup through match completion.\n3. Reset by recreating the database when you need a fresh deterministic dataset.\n\nScope and constraints\n- This module is for non-production environments.\n- Demo records prioritize workflow coverage over real-world data volume.\n- The seeded Spring Cup intentionally omits category and gender restrictions\n  because its participant fixture demonstrates senior, youth, and women's\n  teams in one navigable competition.\n- Data is versioned with the addon and intended to stay reproducible across installs.\n\nValidation checklist\n- Module installs without additional manual data steps.\n- Tournament, roster, and standings flows are navigable from seeded records.\n- Portal/public pages can render at least one realistic competition storyline.\n\n## Release-pilot qualification\n\nThe integrated P0-P3 release path is documented in\n`docs/RELEASE_PILOT_SCENARIO.md`. Run\n`scripts/ci/run_rc_validation.sh focus` before promoting a release candidate.\n\n## Accessible operator training walkthrough\n\nUse the deterministic demo database with a federation manager who also has the\ncompetition administrator, registration manager, competition designer, calendar\nplanner, schedule planner, schedule approver, and match-day manager roles.\n\nComplete the normal path without a mouse:\n\n1. Open **Competition Overview** and move through controls with `Tab` and\n   `Shift+Tab`. The focused control must always have a visible outline.\n2. Continue through **Registration**, **Format**, **Calendar**, **Schedule**, and\n   **Review**, activating links and buttons with `Enter` or `Space`.\n3. Submit an incomplete portal form. Focus must move to the error summary, and\n   invalid controls must reference that summary through `aria-describedby`.\n4. Open and close a confirmation modal. Focus must enter the modal and return to\n   the control that opened it.\n5. Repeat the club portal's competition, roster, officiating, and result tasks at\n   a 390 CSS-pixel viewport. No primary action may require horizontal page\n   scrolling.\n6. Confirm that every state is expressed as readable text. Color and icons may\n   reinforce the state but must not be the only status signal.\n\nThe `keyboard_competition_setup` browser tour qualifies the canonical backend\njourney mechanically. Portal template accessibility and mobile tests qualify\nlabels, error semantics, status text, responsive tables, and action wrapping.\n\n\n## Verified operator menu guide\n\nUse [`docs/COMPETITION_UI_WORKFLOW.md`](../docs/COMPETITION_UI_WORKFLOW.md) during training and acceptance. Addon names are not always visible as menus.\n\n\n## Full competition lifecycle browser tour\n\nThe `full_competition_lifecycle` browser tour follows the maintained operator handoffs from Competition Overview through registration, format, calendar, scheduling, independent review, match-day control, officiating assignment, standings, and the canonical public competition index.  {"content": "# Sports Federation Discipline\n\nIncident reporting, disciplinary case management, sanctions, and player\nsuspensions. Provides the full disciplinary pipeline from incident detection\nthrough case resolution to sanction enforcement.\n\n## Purpose\n\nTracks **incidents** that occur during matches, groups them into **disciplinary\ncases** for investigation, and records **sanctions** (fines, warnings) and\n**suspensions** (match bans) as outcomes. Links back to players, clubs, and\nreferees for comprehensive disciplinary records.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n| Module | Reason |\n|--------|--------|\n| `sports_federation_base` | Clubs |\n| `sports_federation_people` | Players |\n| `sports_federation_tournament` | Matches |\n| `mail` | Chatter |\n\n## Models\n\n### `federation.match.incident`\n\nAn event that occurred during a match that may trigger disciplinary action.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char | Incident title |\n| `match_id` | Many2one | The match |\n| `player_id` | Many2one | Involved player |\n| `club_id` | Many2one | Involved club |\n| `referee_id` | Many2one | Reporting referee |\n| `incident_type` | Selection | warning / yellow_card / red_card / misconduct / violence / admin_issue / other |\n| `minute_text` | Char | Match minute (text for flexibility) |\n| `description` | Text | What happened |\n| `case_id` | Many2one | Linked disciplinary case |\n| `date_reported` | Date | When reported |\n| `reported_by_user_id` | Many2one | System user who filed it |\n| `status` | Selection | new / attached / closed |\n\n### `federation.disciplinary.case`\n\nAn investigation triggered by one or more incidents.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char | Case title |\n| `reference` | Char | Auto-sequence reference number |\n| `state` | Selection | draft / under_review / decided / appealed / closed |\n| `opened_on` / `decided_on` / `closed_on` | Date | Timeline |\n| `responsible_user_id` | Many2one | Case handler |\n| `incident_ids` | One2many | Related incidents |\n| `sanction_ids` | One2many | Resulting sanctions |\n| `suspension_ids` | One2many | Resulting suspensions |\n| `incident_count` / `sanction_count` / `suspension_count` | Integer | Dedicated stat counters for case shortcuts |\n| `subject_player_id` / `subject_club_id` / `subject_referee_id` | Many2one | Subject |\n| `summary` / `notes` | Text | Case details |\n\n- **State machine**: draft → under_review → decided → appealed / closed, with under-review cases allowed back to draft for corrections before a decision is recorded.\n- **Auto-numbering** via `ir.sequence`.\n- **Counter labels** use distinct technical field names so the case relation tabs and their stat counters do not trigger duplicate-label warnings during module loading.\n\n### `federation.sanction`\n\nA penalty imposed as the outcome of a disciplinary case.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char | Sanction title |\n| `case_id` | Many2one | Parent case |\n| `sanction_type` | Selection | fine / warning / ban / point_deduction / other |\n| `player_id` / `club_id` / `referee_id` | Many2one | Who is sanctioned |\n| `amount` / `currency_id` | Monetary | For fines |\n| `effective_date` | Date | When it takes effect |\n| `notes` | Text | Details |\n\n### `federation.suspension`\n\nA time-bound match ban for a player.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char | Suspension title |\n| `case_id` | Many2one | Parent case |\n| `player_id` | Many2one | Suspended player |\n| `date_start` / `date_end` | Date | Ban period |\n| `state` | Selection | active / served / overturned |\n| `notes` | Text | Details |\n\n## Security Groups\n\n| Group | Purpose |\n|-------|---------|\n| Disciplinary Staff | Can manage incidents, cases, sanctions, and suspensions |\n\n## Data Files\n\n| File | Content |\n|------|---------|\n| `data/ir_sequence.xml` | `FED-DISC-` sequence for case reference numbers |\n\n## Key Behaviours\n\n1. **Incident → Case linking** — Incidents can be grouped into a case for joint handling.\n2. **Case lifecycle** — draft → under_review → decided → appealed / closed with date tracking, and under-review cases can be reopened to draft before a decision is recorded.\n3. **Multiple outcomes** — A single case can produce multiple sanctions and suspensions.\n4. **Player integration** — Inherited views add discipline tabs to player forms.\n5. **Match integration** — Inherited views add incident lists to match forms.\n6. **Finance bridge integration** — When `sports_federation_finance_bridge` is installed,\n   sanctions of type `fine` automatically create source-linked finance events and\n   keep draft amounts synchronized with sanction edits.\n", "content_length": 4687, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path":  {"content": "# Sports Federation Format\n\nThe format addon manages versioned competition structures, their stages, and\nFormat Studio stage graphs.\n\n## Stage graph models\n\nFormat Studio uses `federation.structure.stage.progression` for edges between\nstages in one `federation.competition.structure`. This is deliberately\nseparate from the competition engine's `federation.stage.progression` model,\nwhich belongs to tournament-level progression workflows and uses a different\nrelation contract.\n\nBefore generating a structure, the graph is validated for cycles. Root stages\ncan then be prepared; dependent stages wait for incoming progression results.\nApproved fixture results can populate dependent stages, and frozen standings\nare stored as immutable snapshots.\n\nStage-graph access rules are loaded from `security/ir.model.access.csv`. The\nstructure form extension identifies the stage tab by its `stage_ids` field so\nthe view remains safe when translated page labels change.\n## Supported format generation\n\nThe format studio now estimates fixture and round counts before generation. It supports single and double leagues, seeded knockout and placement brackets, match series, pool-to-knockout configuration, championship/relegation splits, Swiss rounds, ladder formats, and power-of-two double elimination. Swiss round counts are configurable on the structure, while double elimination uses the dynamic pairing service to account for its winner, loser, and reset-final routes. These estimates are planning guidance; format-specific generation workflows remain responsible for validating the final fixture graph.\n", "content_length": 1599, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_format/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "a77ea3a8e64ed4bd839025fe8e3e21961d32e160ec3c607bd480eaa5b7eb539d", "size_bytes": 1599}
