 {"content": "# Sports Federation Governance\n\nFormal override-request workflow with decisions and audit trails. Provides a\nstructured way for federation officials to request, review, and implement\nexceptions to standard processes.\n\n## Purpose\n\nSome situations require bending the rules — late registrations, replayed matches,\nexceptional eligibility grants. This module ensures those exceptions are\n**requested, decided, logged, and auditable** rather than happening informally.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n| Module | Reason |\n|--------|--------|\n| `sports_federation_base` | Core entities |\n| `sports_federation_people` | Player references |\n| `sports_federation_tournament` | Tournament references |\n| `mail` | Chatter |\n\n## Models\n\n### `federation.override.request`\n\nA formal request to override a standard process.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char | Request title |\n| `request_type` | Selection | Type of override |\n| `target_model` / `target_res_id` | Char / Integer | Linked record |\n| `requested_by_id` | Many2one | Requester (user) |\n| `requested_on` | Datetime | Request timestamp |\n| `state` | Selection | draft / submitted / approved / rejected / implemented / closed |\n| `reason` | Text | Justification |\n| `implementation_note` | Text | How it was applied |\n| `decision_ids` | One2many | Review decisions |\n| `audit_note_ids` | One2many | Audit trail entries |\n| `outcome_ids` | One2many | Post-decision outcome log |\n\n- **State machine**: draft → submitted → approved / rejected → implemented → closed, with submitted requests withdrawable back to draft before a decision is recorded.\n\n### `federation.override.decision`\n\nA review decision on an override request.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `request_id` | Many2one | The request |\n| `decision` | Selection | approve / reject / request_info |\n| `decided_by_id` | Many2one | Decision maker |\n| `decided_on` | Datetime | Decision timestamp |\n| `note` | Text | Reasoning |\n\n### `federation.audit.note`\n\nFree-form audit notes attached to an override request.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `request_id` | Many2one | The request |\n| `note` | Text | Audit remark |\n| `author_id` | Many2one | Author |\n| `created_on` | Datetime | Timestamp |\n\n### `federation.override.outcome`\n\nOutcome tracking row attached to an override request after implementation or\nfollow-up review.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `request_id` | Many2one | Source override request |\n| `outcome` | Selection | implemented / effective / partial / ineffective / reversed |\n| `outcome_on` | Datetime | When the outcome was recorded |\n| `recorded_by_id` | Many2one | Operator recording the outcome |\n| `request_type` | Selection | Snapshot of the originating request type |\n| `target_model` / `target_res_id` | Char / Integer | Snapshot of the overridden record |\n| `request_state` | Selection | Request state at the time of logging |\n| `note` | Text | Outcome commentary |\n\n## Security Groups\n\n| Group | Purpose |\n|-------|---------|\n| Governance Officer | Can review and decide on override requests |\n\n## Key Behaviours\n\n1. **Formal request lifecycle** — Every exception starts as a draft request,\n   can be withdrawn back to draft while still submitted, and otherwise follows\n   a structured approval flow.\n2. **Multi-decision support** — Multiple governance officers can weigh in on a\n   single request.\n3. **Audit trail** — All decisions and notes are timestamped and attributed.\n4. **Generic target** — Requests can link to any record type via model/res_id.\n5. **Outcome evidence** — implemented requests now create outcome-log rows so\n   governance review can extend beyond the approval moment.\n", "content_length": 3754, +{"content": "# Sports Federation Officiating\n\nVersion: 19.0.1.6.0\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-08-20\nReview cadence: Every release\n\nReferee records, certifications, match assignments, club referee duties, reimbursement requests, and competition-workspace readiness checks.\n\n## Responsibilities\n\n- referee profiles and qualification data\n- match referee assignments and response lifecycle\n- club referee-duty nominations\n- officiating readiness validation\n- reimbursement request workflow\n- portal and backend actions through the portal addon integration\n\n## Competition integration\n\nThe addon extends competition validation through the documented workspace extension contract. Officiating readiness should block or warn at the appropriate lifecycle stage without preventing early schedule construction.\n\n## Security\n\nOfficials may only access assignments linked to their portal identity. Club representatives may only manage duties inside their authorized club or team scope. Federation managers retain administrative control.\n\n## Tests\n\nCoverage includes assignment lifecycle, duties, reimbursements, portal access, match-day tours, and workspace integration.\n\n## ownership\n\nOfficial assignments and club-supplied duties belong to fixture-backed\noperational matches. Use **Officiating → Plan Match-Day Officials** to assign a\nfederation referee or generate club duties for every applicable match in the\ncurrent live publication. The removed round wizard must not be reintroduced.\n\n\n## Automatic club-duty allocation\n\nFrom **Match Operations → Officiating → Plan Match-Day Officials**, select **Auto-assign Club Duties** for a published match day. The default policy requests four roles per match and assigns all missing roles for that match to one participating club.\n\nThe allocator is deterministic and balances the accumulated duty count across eligible clubs. It excludes the two clubs playing the target match. By default it also prefers clubs that have no team playing during the target match window; matches on different courts are treated as concurrent when their published time windows overlap. A configurable fallback can use the least-loaded conflicted club when no non-playing club exists. Disable that fallback when the competition requires a strict non-playing-team rule.\n\n**Preserve existing assignments** is enabled by default. Existing active federation or volunteer referee assignments and existing club duties satisfy their role and are never overwritten. The wizard creates only the missing roles. Duties can be opened immediately for club nomination, or left in draft for operator review.\n", "content_length": 2620, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_officiating/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "c4a24f6ae77f112e96fdb9f4327c2f3364a48540661df4d4231b677a08ae7fb9", "size_bytes": 2626}

 {"content": "# Sports Federation People\n\nPlayer master data and license management for the federation. Tracks every\nregistered player's personal information, club affiliation, and maintains a\ncomplete licensing history across seasons.\n\n## Purpose\n\nProvides the **player** and **player license** models that underpin roster\nmanagement, eligibility checks, discipline tracking, and compliance workflows.\nEvery module that deals with individual athletes depends on People.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- `sports_federation_base`: Clubs, teams, and seasons.\n\n## Models\n\n### `federation.player`\n\nMaster record for every registered individual. Names are split into first/last\nfor sorting and flexible display.\n\n- `name`: Char (computed), stored as `last_name, first_name`.\n- `first_name` / `last_name`: Char, legal name parts and both required.\n- `birth_date`: Date of birth.\n- `gender`: Selection with `male`, `female`, or `other`.\n- `nationality_id`: Many2one to the nationality country.\n- `club_id`: Many2one to the current club affiliation.\n- `team_ids`: Many2many teams the player belongs to.\n- `email` / `phone` / `mobile`: Contact channels.\n- `photo`: Binary player photograph.\n- `state`: Selection with `draft`, `active`, `suspended`, or `retired`.\n- `license_ids`: One2many historical license records.\n- `license_count`: Integer stat-button counter.\n- `notes`: Free-form notes.\n\n- **State machine**: draft → active → suspended / retired.\n- **Stat button** navigates to license history.\n\n### `federation.player.license`\n\nSeason-scoped license that proves a player's right to compete. A player may hold\nmultiple licenses across seasons, but only one active license per season applies.\n\n- `name`: Char, auto-generated license number from a sequence.\n- `player_id`: Many2one to the licensed player.\n- `season_id`: Many2one to the covered season.\n- `club_id`: Many2one to the club at time of issue.\n- `issue_date` / `expiry_date`: Date validity window.\n- `state`: Selection with `draft`, `active`, `expired`, or `cancelled`.\n- `category`: Selection for license category such as amateur or professional.\n- `eligibility_notes`: Text eligibility remarks.\n- `notes`: Additional notes.\n\n- License numbers generated via `ir.sequence`.\n- Operator-facing copy should use `cancelled` for invalidated licenses. Older\n   notes may still say `revoked`, but that is compatibility-only wording.\n\n## Data Files\n\n- `data/ir_sequence.xml`: `FED-LIC-` sequence for license numbers.\n- `security/ir.model.access.csv`: CRUD rights for federation groups.\n\n## Key Behaviours\n\n1. **Name computation** — `name` is automatically composed from `last_name` and\n   `first_name` and kept in sync.\n2. **License numbering** — Every new license receives an auto-incremented\n   `FED-LIC-XXXXX` reference via `ir.sequence`.\n3. **Club ↔ Player link** — `club_id` on the player is the *current* affiliation;\n   the license records preserve the historical club at time of issue.\n", "content_length": 2915, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_people/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "28909238ab4d7553ba5922d32d0c903d7ecd966f88949edb478d180d463fa738", "size_bytes": 2927}

 {"content": "# Sports Federation Club Roles and Portal\n\nVersion: 19.0.4.1.0\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-08-23\nReview cadence: Every release\n\nRole-oriented self-service portal for club representatives, officials, and tournament operators.\n\n## Primary user journeys\n\n### Club representative\n\n- manage club teams and players\n- submit season and tournament registrations\n- prepare and activate rosters\n- complete match sheets and readiness tasks\n- nominate officials\n- review result actions and deadlines\n\n### Official\n\n- view assignments\n- confirm or decline within the authorized scope\n- access relevant match information\n\n### Tournament operator\n\n- use the tournament operations board\n- monitor courts, matches, readiness, and action queues\n- execute scoped result and operational actions\n\n## Trust boundary\n\nAll privileged portal writes must use a model-owned method and the shared `federation.portal.privilege` boundary. Controllers validate input and resolve scope but do not perform raw elevated business writes. See `adr/0001-portal-trust-boundaries.md`.\n\nEvery new privileged route requires:\n\n1. positive in-scope coverage\n2. negative out-of-scope coverage\n3. direct-ID or guessed-record coverage\n4. model/helper ownership assertions when elevation is used\n5. CSRF enforcement for state-changing browser or JSON-RPC routes\n\n## Portal UX direction\n\nThe landing page should remain task-first. Common tasks are teams, registrations, upcoming matches, and action items. Specialist tools should be progressively disclosed instead of presented as an undifferentiated module catalogue.\n\n## Operations board\n\nThe board loads through scoped JSON-RPC, supports polling and structured failures, and exposes only matches and actions available to the current user. Server-side checks remain authoritative.\n\n## Tests\n\nThe module includes HTTP smoke, ownership, access-denied, team, player, roster, registration, officiating, result, accessibility, mobile, operations-board, and end-to-end portal workflow tests.\n\n## Consolidated documentation\n\n`PORTAL_OWNERSHIP_COVERAGE.md`, `PORTAL_OWNERSHIP_TEST_MATRIX.md`, and `ROADMAP_RC.md` are deleted. Their durable rules are consolidated here and in ADR-0001; the test files are the authoritative live coverage map.\n\n## competition portal\n\nThe active competition portal is edition-based. Participation comes from\ncompetition entries and finalized participant sets. Match-day schedule data is\nrendered only from each match day's current live publication. Draft schedules,\nreview evidence and superseded publications are intentionally unavailable.\n\nPrimary routes:\n\n- `/my/competitions`\n- `/my/competition-entries`\n- `/my/match-days`\n- `/sports/match-days/<id>/operations`\n\nLegacy tournament workspace routes are redirect-only and render no V1 data.\nThe backend tournament-registration action is loaded before the menus that use\nit, so a fresh module install and an upgrade both build the registration menu\nwithout relying on stale database metadata.\n\n\n## Accessible error recovery and focus management\n\nPortal forms move keyboard focus to server-rendered error summaries, connect\ninvalid controls to that summary with `aria-describedby`, and announce the\nsummary through an assertive live region. Bootstrap confirmation dialogs move\nfocus into the dialog and restore it to the invoking control when closed.\nKeyboard focus uses a visible outline that does not depend on color-only status\ncues. The focused accessibility suite covers these contracts together with\nmobile table and action wrapping.\n\n\n## Club competition data tutorial\n\nClub representatives use **My Account > Data API** (`/my/data-api`) for live URLs, curl and JavaScript examples, privacy rules, and caching guidance.\n", "content_length": 3727, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_portal/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "20882b3c9483b628db1e4dd12c84940bfd66b2b4f9416ade24df2df785f0e97f", "size_bytes": 3727}

published tournament queries,\nteam/result/standings/schedule datasets, JSON feed payloads, and ICS calendar\nexport content.\n\n### `federation.team`\n\n| Field | Type | Description team-linked\nhighlights without editing website templates. Scheduling requires a publish\nstart while the item is still in draft; items can publish from draft or\nscheduled, archive from scheduled or published, and reset from scheduled or\narchived back to draft.\n\n### `federation.standing`\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `website_published` | Boolean | Allows standings publication |\n| `public_title` | Char | Public-facing table title |\n\n## Controllers\n\n### `PublicTournamentHubController`\n\nCanonical public routes use one namespace only:\n\n| Route | Auth | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `GET /competitions` | public | Competition hub |\n| `POST /competitions/api/json` | public | Published competition discovery |\n| `GET /competitions/<edition-slug>` | public | Competition overview with published divisions |\n| `GET /competitions/<edition-slug>/format` | public | Published format and bracket information |\n| `GET /competitions/<edition-slug>/schedule` | public | Published competition schedule |\n| `GET /competitions/<edition-slug>/gamedays/<matchday-id>` | public | Published game-day board |\n| `GET /competitions/<edition-slug>/register?division_id=<division-id>` | user | Club registration form |\n| `POST /competitions/<edition-slug>/register?division_id=<division-id>` | user | Club registration submission |\n| `GET /competitions/<edition-slug>/divisions/<division-slug>/schedule.ics` | public | Division calendar export |\n| `GET /api/v1/competitions` | public | Published competition API index |\n| `GET /api/v1/competitions/<edition-slug>` | public | Complete published competition feed |\n| `GET /teams/<slug>` | public | Public team profile |\n\nThere are no tournament-named or numeric compatibility routes. The product had not been released when the namespace was consolidated, so only `/competitions` is supported.\n\n### `PublicFollowController`\n\nCanonical follow and discovery routes:\n\n| Route | Auth | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `GET /seasons` | public | Season discovery page for published seasons |\n| `GET /seasons/<slug>` | public | Canonical season landing page with editorial and tournament sections |\n| `GET /teams/<slug>/schedule` | public | Team-centric grouped upcoming schedule |\n| `GET /teams/<slug>/results` | public | Team-centric recent approved results |\n| `GET /teams/<slug>/schedule.ics` | public | Team schedule calendar export |\n| `GET /api/v1/teams/<slug>/feed` | public | Stable v1 team follow feed |\n\n## Public-site behaviour\n\n1. Tournament-first navigation: the visible website now centers tournaments and nests published coverage under the existing Tournaments area.\n2. Slug-first URLs: tournaments and teams use canonical slug routes, with numeric routes preserved only for backward compatibility.\n3. Editorial control: operators can feature tournaments, add summaries, pin announcements, and assign hero imagery without editing templates.\n4. Better hub discovery: the main hub separates featured, live, recent, and archived tournaments instead of showing one flat list.\n5. Team-aware public pages: standings, results, schedule, and teams pages link through to public team profiles when available.\n6. Sticky section navigation: tournament sub-pages share one consistent local navigation model.\n7. Calendar export: schedules can be consumed as `.ics` for personal or club calendars.\n8. Stable feed contract: the v1 feed includes slug-aware public URLs alongside tournament, standings, schedule, bracket, and result data.\n9. Visibility enforcement: results and standings respect per-tournament publication toggles.\n10. Sanitized website rendering: public descriptions and website content render through standard website field handling.\n11. Backward compatibility: legacy competition routes keep resolving while the visible product language is tournament-first.\n12. Season discovery and editorial planning: published seasons aggregate featured tournaments, recent tournaments, and live editorial items with publication windows.\n13. Automatic menu cleanup: module installs and upgrades normalize stale `/competitions` website menus into the Tournaments submenu and remove leftover duplicates.\n14. Shared privileged-write boundary: website registration POST routes validate HTTP input and then reuse the same tournament registration helper as the portal layer.\n15. Publication handoff guidance: tournament and standings Website tabs now explain whether visibility is blocked by tournament publication, missing standings, unpublished standings, or disabled standings toggles, with direct links back to standings when operators need to act there.\n\n## Publication guards\n\n- Controllers resolve tournaments, seasons, and team public routes through publication- and visibility-scoped queries before canonical redirects, page rendering, feed reads, or registration handling.\n- Unpublished tournaments lose public access immediately, regardless of related data still present in the database.\n- Legacy numeric compatibility routes redirect only while the tournament still satisfies the relevant public visibility guard.\n- Season slug and numeric detail routes only resolve website-published seasons.\n- Team profile, schedule, results, ICS, and feed routes only resolve teams with a published competition footprint.\n- Public results are limited to approved results.\n- Public participant lists exclude withdrawn entries.\n- Standings exposure depends on both tournament publication and the standings visibility controls.\n\n\n## Public controller boundaries\n\nRoute orchestration lives in `public_competitions.py`. Framework response, canonical resolution, authenticated club lookup, error redirect, and rate-limit response behavior live in `_public_request.py`. New domain queries belong in model query services rather than either controller helper.\n\n\n## Complete competition API\n\n`GET /api/v1/competitions` lists published competitions; `GET /api/v1/competitions/<edition-slug>` aggregates every published division and its public teams, schedules, approved results, standings, brackets, and links.\n\n## Competition route upgrade safety\n\nThe `19.0.3.0.0` pre-migration repairs the stored selector of the competition-hub editorial extension before Odoo reloads its parent template. This prevents databases upgraded from the former route namespace from failing registry initialization while the canonical `/competitions` templates are loaded. Fresh installations already use the canonical selector and require no special action.\n", "content_length": 9985, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_public_site/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "8554edeb303f783288fd939fb762b27693a009ae6f7ed9b3fb93b191d7a6833d", "size_bytes": 9985}

Tournament-first navigation: the visible website now centers tournaments and nests published coverage under the existing Tournaments area.\n2. Slug-first URLs: tournaments and teams use canonical slug routes, with numeric routes preserved only for backward compatibility.\n3. Editorial control: operators can feature tournaments, add summaries, pin announcements, and assign hero imagery without editing templates.\n4. Better hub discovery: the main hub separates featured, live, recent, and archived tournaments instead of showing one flat list.\n5. Team-aware public pages: standings, results, schedule, and teams pages link through to public team profiles when available.\n6. Sticky section navigation: tournament sub-pages share one consistent local navigation model.\n7. Calendar export: schedules can be consumed as `.ics` for personal or club calendars.\n8. Stable feed contract: the v1 feed includes slug-aware public URLs alongside tournament, standings, schedule, bracket, and result data.\n9. Visibility enforcement: results and standings respect per-tournament publication toggles.\n10. Sanitized website rendering: public descriptions and website content render through standard website field handling.\n11. Backward compatibility: legacy competition routes keep resolving while the visible product language is tournament-first.\n12. Season discovery and editorial planning: published seasons aggregate featured tournaments, recent tournaments, and live editorial items with publication windows.\n13. Automatic menu cleanup: module installs and upgrades normalize stale `/competitions` website menus into the Tournaments submenu and remove leftover duplicates.\n14. Shared privileged-write boundary: website registration POST routes validate HTTP input and then reuse the same tournament registration helper as the portal layer.\n15. Registration feedback redirects preserve the division selector query parameter, so capacity and validation messages return to the correct registration form.\n16. Publication handoff guidance: tournament and standings Website tabs now explain whether visibility is blocked by tournament publication, missing standings, unpublished standings, or disabled standings toggles, with direct links back to standings when operators need to act there.\n\n## Publication guards\n\n- Controllers resolve tournaments, seasons, and team public routes through publication- and visibility-scoped queries before canonical redirects, page rendering, feed reads, or registration handling.\n- Unpublished tournaments lose public access immediately, regardless of related data still present in the database.\n- Legacy numeric compatibility routes redirect only while the tournament still satisfies the relevant public visibility guard.\n- Season slug and numeric detail routes only resolve website-published seasons.\n- Team profile, schedule, results, ICS, and feed routes only resolve teams with a published competition footprint.\n- Public results are limited to approved results.\n- Public participant lists exclude withdrawn entries.\n- Standings exposure depends on both tournament publication and the standings visibility controls.\n\n\n## Public controller boundaries\n\nRoute orchestration lives in `public_competitions.py`. Framework response, canonical resolution, authenticated club lookup, error redirect, and rate-limit response behavior live in `_public_request.py`. New domain queries belong in model query services rather than either controller helper.\n\n\n## Complete competition API\n\n`GET /api/v1/competitions` lists published competitions; `GET /api/v1/competitions/<edition-slug>` aggregates every published division and its public teams, schedules, approved results, standings, brackets, and links.\n\n## Competition route upgrade safety\n\nThe `19.0.3.0.0` pre-migration repairs the stored selector of the competition-hub editorial extension before Odoo reloads its parent template. This prevents databases upgraded from the former route namespace from failing registry initialization while the canonical `/competitions` templates are loaded. -{"content": "# Schedule Approval\n\nThis addon owns independent schedule review and immutable schedule publication.\nIt does not own working assignments, calendar capacity, or match-day execution.\n\n## Operator flow\n\n1. A schedule planner submits a complete schedule from **Schedule Planner**.\n2. The addon creates immutable review evidence and opens the pending review.\n3. A different assigned schedule approver opens **Schedule Review Queue**.\n4. The approver either enters a note and selects **Request Changes**, or selects\n   **Approve Schedule**.\n5. Approved reviews appear under **Publication > Approved Schedules**.\n6. **Publish Schedule** creates any missing operational matches for the assigned\n   fixtures through the fixture materializer, creates an immutable publication,\n   links matches to their exact slots, and makes the publication current for the\n   match day.\n7. **Publication > Schedule Publications** retains live and superseded evidence.\n\nThe command service enforces edition roles, separation of duties, submitted\nrevision equality, snapshot-digest equality for schedule facts, and schedule\nrevalidation. Operational match links are derived and may be materialized at\npublication. Buttons are only orchestration entry points and never duplicate\nthe business rules.\nEach review records the authenticated schedule planner who submits it, so that\nplanner can withdraw a pending review before an approver decides it.\nRole assignments remain administrator-managed; the Schedule Approver group\nexposes the workflow actions, while a per-edition `schedule_approver` assignment\nauthorizes the operation. The role check performs a read-only internal lookup,\nand approval revalidation performs controlled read-only access to the submitted\ncalendar and venue data, so approvers do not need CRUD access to those\nadministrator-managed records. Reviewers may edit the note while a review is\npending; state and audit fields remain command-service-only.\n\n## Tests and contracts\n\n```bash\npython ci/check_competition_pipeline_contract.py\npython ci/check_schedule_handoff_contract.py\nbash ci/run_tests.sh --module sports_federation_schedule_approval\nbash ci/run_tests.sh --suite competition_core\n```\n\n## 5.1.1 integrity rules\n\nReview evidence is immutable through the model guard. +{"content": "# Schedule Approval\n\nThis addon owns independent schedule review and immutable schedule publication.\nIt does not own working assignments, calendar capacity, or match-day execution.\n\n## Operator flow\n\n1. A schedule planner submits a complete schedule from **Schedule Planner**.\n2. The addon creates immutable review evidence and opens the pending review.\n3. A different assigned schedule approver opens **Schedule Review Queue**.\n4. The approver either enters a note and selects **Request Changes**, or selects\n   **Approve Schedule**.\n5. Approved reviews appear under **Publication > Approved Schedules**.\n6. **Publish Schedule** creates any missing operational matches for the assigned\n   fixtures through the fixture materializer, creates an immutable publication,\n   links matches to their exact slots, and makes the publication current for the\n   match day.\n7. **Publication > Schedule Publications** retains live and superseded evidence.\n\nThe command service enforces edition roles, separation of duties, submitted\nrevision equality, snapshot-digest equality for schedule facts, and schedule\nrevalidation. Operational match links are derived and may be materialized at\npublication. Buttons are only orchestration entry points and never duplicate\nthe business rules.\nEach review records the authenticated schedule planner who submits it, so that\nplanner can withdraw a pending review before an approver decides it.\nRole assignments remain administrator-managed; the Schedule Approver group\nexposes the workflow actions, while a per-edition `schedule_approver` assignment\nauthorizes the operation. The role check performs a read-only internal lookup,\nand approval revalidation performs controlled read-only access to the submitted\ncalendar and venue data, so approvers do not need CRUD access to those\nadministrator-managed records. Reviewers may edit the note while a review is\npending; state and audit fields remain command-service-only.\n\n## Tests and contracts\n\n```bash\npython ci/check_competition_pipeline_contract.py\npython ci/check_schedule_handoff_contract.py\nbash ci/run_tests.sh --module sports_federation_schedule_approval\nbash ci/run_tests.sh --suite competition_core\n```\n\n## 5.1.1 integrity rules\n\nReview evidence is immutable through the model guard. Pending reviewers may edit\nonly the note; only the approval command service can write decision fields\nthrough a narrowly scoped context. Publications are live,\nversioned and replaced per match day, not per edition. Publication confirmation\nlocks the match day and verifies the expected current publication before\nallocating the next version. Replacements require a dedicated reason that is\nseparate from the review note.\n\n\n## Expanded match-day publication guard\n\nImmediately before replacing a live publication, the approval service validates the approved schedule against every fixture currently allocated to the physical match day. A division or fixture added after review invalidates that review for publication purposes. The planner must refresh the schedule, assign the newly exposed fixtures, and submit the complete replacement for review again. This guarantees that Match-Day Control and public publishing consume one complete multi-division publication.\n", "content_length": 3231, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_schedule_approval/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "faf496085aa52559da986e3f70bf9e58588aea7c2c2e5b761a31300c46b0aa88", "size_bytes": 3231}

 {"content": "# Sports Federation Tournament\n\nTournament lifecycle management — from creation through scheduling to completion.\nProvides the structural backbone for all competitive activity: tournaments, stages,\ngroups, participants, and matches.\n\n## Purpose\n\nModels the full **tournament hierarchy**: a tournament is divided into stages\n(e.g. group phase, quarter-finals), stages contain groups, and groups contain\nmatches between participants. This module is the central hub that most\ncompetition-related modules extend.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n| Module | Reason |\n|--------|--------|\n| `sports_federation_base` | Clubs, teams, seasons |\n| `sports_federation_rules` | Rule sets, competitions |\n\n## Models\n\n### `federation.competition`\n\nA named competition series (e.g. \"National League Division 1\") that may span\nmultiple seasons and link to a rule set.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` / `code` | Char | Competition identity |\n| `season_id` | Many2one | Governing season |\n| `rule_set_id` | Many2one | Applicable rule set |\n| `state` | Selection | draft / active / closed |\n| `tournament_ids` | One2many | Tournaments under this competition |\n\n### `federation.season` extension\n\nThe module extends seasons with a tournament relation and a dedicated tournament\ncount stat used by the season form shortcut into related tournaments.\n\n### `federation.tournament`\n\nA single tournament event within a competition or season.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` / `code` | Char | Tournament identity |\n| `season_id` | Many2one | Season context |\n| `competition_id` | Many2one | Parent competition |\n| `rule_set_id` | Many2one | Rules (inherited from competition or set directly) |\n| `tournament_type` | Selection | league / cup / friendly / playoff |\n| `state` | Selection | draft / open / in_progress / closed / cancelled |\n| `date_start` / `date_end` | Date | Event window |\n| `max_participants` | Integer | Participant cap |\n| `stage_ids` | One2many | Tournament stages |\n| `participant_ids` | One2many | Enrolled participants |\n| `match_ids` | One2many | All matches across stages |\n\n- **State machine**: draft → open → in_progress → closed / cancelled.\n- **Stat buttons** for stages, participants, and matches.\n\n### `federation.tournament.stage`\n\nA phase or round within a tournament (e.g. \"Group Phase\", \"Semi-finals\").\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char | Stage label |\n| `tournament_id` | Many2one | Parent tournament |\n| `stage_type` | Selection | group / knockout / playoff / other |\n| `sequence` | Integer | Natural ordering |\n| `date_start` / `date_end` | Date | Stage window |\n| `group_ids` | One2many | Groups within this stage |\n| `match_ids` | One2many | Matches in this stage |\n\n### `federation.tournament.group`\n\nA subdivision within a stage (e.g. \"Group A\", \"Pool 1\").\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char | Group label |\n| `stage_id` | Many2one | Parent stage |\n| `tournament_id` | Many2one | Computed from stage |\n| `sequence` | Integer | Natural ordering |\n| `max_participants` | Integer | Group capacity |\n| `participant_ids` | One2many | Teams in this group |\n| `match_ids` | One2many | Group matches |\n\n### `federation.tournament.participant`\n\nLinks a team to a tournament, optionally assigned to a specific stage and group.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char (computed) | Team name in tournament context |\n| `tournament_id` | Many2one | Tournament |\n| `team_id` | Many2one | The team |\n| `club_id` | Many2one | Computed from team |\n| `stage_id` / `group_id` | Many2one | Assignment |\n| `seed` | Integer | Seeding rank |\n| `registration_date` | Date | When enrolled |\n| `state` | Selection | registered / confirmed / withdrawn / eliminated |\n\n### `federation.match`\n\nAn individual game between two teams.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char (computed) | \"Home vs Away\" |\n| `tournament_id` | Many2one | Tournament |\n| `stage_id` / `group_id` | Many2one | Location in hierarchy |\n| `round_id` | Many2one | Single-day round assignment |\n| `home_team_id` / `away_team_id` | Many2one | Competing teams |\n| `date_scheduled` | Datetime | Stored kickoff datetime for downstream integrations |\n| `scheduled_date` | Date (computed) | Inherited from the assigned round |\n| `scheduled_time` | Float | Editable match kickoff time-of-day |\n| `home_score` / `away_score` | Integer | Final score |\n| `state` | Selection | draft / scheduled / in_progress / done / cancelled |\n\n- **State machine**: draft → scheduled → in_progress → done / cancelled.\n\n## Key Behaviours\n\n1. **Hierarchical structure** — Tournament → Stage → Group → Match.\n2. **Participant tracking** — Teams enrol in a tournament and are placed into stages/groups.\n3. **Score entry** — Match results are recorded with home/away scores.\n4. **State management** — Both tournaments and matches follow state machines that\n   prevent illogical transitions.\n5. **Round-owned scheduling** — Rounds are single-day containers. A match assigned to a round inherits that round's calendar date and only stores its own kickoff time.\n6. **Stage windows** — Stages remain the broader multi-day grouping above rounds.\n7. **Tournament open/start guards** — Only active draft tournaments linked to a season can open, and only open tournaments with at least one stage can start.\n8. **Archive safety** — Open or in-progress tournaments must be closed or cancelled before archiving.\n9. **Venue extensions** — Venue fields are supplied by `sports_federation_venues`; this module keeps the core match lifecycle and hierarchy only.\n\n## Migration note (v19.0.1.1.0)\n\n- Added migration scripts under `migrations/19.0.1.1.0/` to harden `federation.match` indexing for high-traffic filters.\n- Added backfill for `scheduled_date` and `round_number` on historical match rows where those persisted values were missing.\n- Added composite indexes for `(tournament_id, state)`, `(stage_id, state)`, `(group_id, state)`, `(scheduled_date, state)`, and `(date_scheduled, state)`.\n\n## Knockout result resolution (v19.0.1.2.0)\n\nKnockout matches must have an unambiguous advancing team before they can be\ncompleted. A tied numeric score requires a non-regulation resolution, such as\novertime, tiebreak, forfeit, walkover, or an administrative decision, plus an\nexplicit advancing team selected from the two match participants.\n\nWinner and loser bracket progression uses this explicit decision, preventing a\ncompleted knockout match from leaving downstream participants unresolved.\n", "content_length": 6639, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_tournament/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "3bf73f9207c54b0d3b527f74a84d44b7e21e216f6a3f91489177bce88e6b76a3", "size_bytes": 6677}

 {"content": "Sports Federation Venues\n========================\n\nVenue, playing-area, and round scheduling support. Tracks physical locations\nwhere matches are held, including address, capacity, facilities, individual\nplaying surfaces, and round-level venue assignment.\n\nPurpose\n-------\n\nCentralizes venue information so tournaments, rounds, and matches can use\nstructured location data instead of free-text fields. Playing areas let a\nsingle venue, such as a sports complex, contain multiple usable surfaces.\nRounds carry the shared schedule metadata for a block of matches: the calendar\ndate and venue live on the round, while each match keeps its own exact kickoff\ntime.\n\nDependencies\n------------\n\n- ``sports_federation_base``: Core entities.\n- ``sports_federation_tournament``: Tournaments and matches.\n\nModels\n------\n\n``federation.venue``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nA physical location such as a stadium, sports hall, or complex.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``name`` (Char): Venue name.\n- ``street`` through ``country_id`` (Address): Full postal address.\n- ``contact_name`` / ``contact_email`` / ``contact_phone`` (Char): On-site\n  contact details.\n- ``capacity`` (Integer): Total spectator capacity.\n- ``equipment_notes`` (Text): Available equipment.\n- ``playing_area_ids`` (One2many): Courts, pitches, and other playable areas.\n- ``blackout_window_ids`` (One2many): Venue or playing-area blackout windows.\n- ``playing_area_count`` (Integer): Stat-button counter.\n- ``blackout_window_count`` (Integer): Stat-button counter.\n- ``notes`` (Text): General notes.\n- ``active`` (Boolean): Whether the venue is in use.\n\n``federation.playing.area``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nA single playing surface within a venue.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``name`` (Char): Area label such as ``Pitch 1``.\n- ``venue_id`` (Many2one): Parent venue.\n- ``code`` (Char): Short code.\n- ``capacity`` (Integer): Surface-specific capacity.\n- ``surface_type`` (Selection): ``grass``, ``artificial``, ``indoor``,\n  ``clay``, or ``other``.\n- ``capability_ids`` (Many2many): Capability tags such as lighting,\n  streaming, or sport-specific equipment.\n- ``active`` (Boolean): Whether the area is available.\n- ``notes`` (Text): Remarks.\n\n``federation.playing.area.capability``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nA reusable tag that describes what a playing area can support.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``name`` (Char): Capability label.\n- ``code`` (Char): Stable short code.\n- ``description`` (Text): Optional operator notes.\n\n``federation.venue.blackout``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nA closure or blackout window that makes a venue or one playing area unavailable.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``name`` (Char): Operator-facing label.\n- ``venue_id`` (Many2one): Affected venue.\n- ``playing_area_id`` (Many2one): Optional specific playing area.\n- ``date_start`` / ``date_end`` (Datetime): Closed interval.\n- ``reason`` (Selection): ``blackout``, ``maintenance``, or ``other``.\n- ``notes`` (Text): Optional scheduling notes.\n\nInherited Extensions\n--------------------\n\n- ``federation.tournament`` gains ``venue_id`` and ``venue_notes`` for\n  tournament-wide venue planning notes plus\n  ``required_playing_area_capability_ids`` for divisions that need specific\n  courts.\n- ``federation.tournament.stage`` surfaces linked ``round_ids`` so stage admins\n  can plan sequence, date, and venue directly on rounds.\n- ``federation.tournament.round`` gains ``venue_id`` alongside the base\n  ``round_date`` field from the tournament module.\n- ``federation.match`` gains ``venue_id`` and ``playing_area_id``. When a\n  match is linked to a round, the round becomes the authoritative shared\n  venue/date scope.\n\nKey Behaviours\n--------------\n\n- **Structured addresses**: venues store full addresses with country\n  references.\n- **Multi-area venues**: a sports complex can have several pitches or courts.\n- **Constraint windows**: venues can declare blackout or maintenance windows at\n  venue or playing-area level.\n- **Capability tags**: playing areas can advertise the operational capabilities\n  they support, and divisions can require matching capabilities.\n- **Round-owned schedule planning**: administrators can create stage rounds up\n  front and assign a date and venue to each one without duplicating scheduling\n  concepts.\n- **Match to round consistency**: assigning a round to a match propagates the\n  tournament and stage scope, applies the round venue, and rejects conflicting\n  venue or date combinations.\n- **Duplicate-pairing guardrails**: teams in the same category cannot play the\n  same opponent more than once inside the same round.\n- **Scheduling integration**: blackout windows, maintenance closures, and\n  capability mismatches are validated by the scheduling workflow before a\n  schedule can be approved.\n- **Finance bridge integration**: when ``sports_federation_finance_bridge`` is\n  installed, scheduling a match with a venue automatically creates or reuses a\n  draft venue-booking charge for passthrough settlement.\n", "content_length": 4924, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_venues/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "b38573da273084eef42de4ea8ae7e354571452133d458891a505ba27574d36fd", "size_bytes": 4924}

+
+# Federation Backend Navigation
+
+Owner: Federation Platform Team
+Last verified against menu XML: 2026-09-04
+Review cadence: Every release
+
+## Goal
+
+The Federation backend is organized around operator intent, not addon names or implementation layers. A user should be able to decide where to go from the business task they are performing. The root navigation therefore has seven stable work areas:
+
+1. **Competitions**: define, create, register, structure, schedule, and review competitions.
+2. **Clubs & People**: maintain clubs, teams, players, licenses, representatives, and season registrations.
+3. **Match Operations**: run match days and manage fixtures, match sheets, venues, officials, and discipline.
+4. **Publishing**: expose approved schedules, standings, and editorial content.
+5. **Finance & Assurance**: manage finance, compliance, and governed exceptions.
+6. **Insights**: review readiness, performance, assurance signals, trends, and scheduled reports.
+7. **Administration**: process operational tasks, integrations, notifications, retention, and technical job health.
+
+## Design rules
+
+- Root tabs represent durable business responsibilities. They must not mirror addon names.
+- A record has one primary navigation home. Cross-links on forms may provide shortcuts, but duplicate root entries are avoided.
+- Daily workflow entries precede configuration and technical records.
+- Technical and audit records remain available, but are grouped at the end of their owning area.
+- Manager-only items stay role-gated. Reparenting a menu must not broaden its groups or model access.
+- Empty compatibility categories are not retained. Existing XML IDs are reused where practical so upgrades move menus instead of creating duplicates.
+- New menus must fit one of the seven work areas. Adding another root tab requires an update to this document and the navigation contract check.
+
+## Intended menu map
+
+```text
+Federation
+├── Competitions
+│   ├── Seasons
+│   ├── Season Competitions
+│   ├── Competition Operations
+│   │   ├── Create Competition
+│   │   ├── Competition Overview
+│   │   ├── Registration Desk
+│   │   ├── Format Studio
+│   │   ├── Calendar Planner
+│   │   ├── Schedule Planner
+│   │   ├── Schedule Review Queue
+│   │   └── Audit & Technical Records
+│   ├── Competition Templates
+│   ├── Format Templates
+│   ├── Rules & Policies
+│   └── Competition Records
+├── Clubs & People
+│   ├── Club Directory
+│   ├── Players & Licensing
+│   ├── Representatives & Access
+│   └── Season Registrations
+├── Match Operations
+│   ├── Match-Day Control
+│   ├── Matches
+│   ├── Match Sheets
+│   ├── Officiating
+│   ├── Venues
+│   └── Discipline
+├── Publishing
+│   ├── Approved Schedules
+│   ├── Schedule Publications
+│   ├── Standings
+│   └── Public Editorial
+├── Finance & Assurance
+│   ├── Finance
+│   ├── Compliance
+│   └── Governance
+├── Insights
+│   └── Reports & Insights
+│       ├── Overview & Readiness
+│       ├── Performance
+│       ├── Assurance & Exceptions
+│       └── Automation & History
+└── Administration
+    ├── Action Queue
+    ├── Notification Centre
+    ├── Imports & Integrations
+    └── System Health
+```
+
+Menus hidden by security groups are omitted for users who do not own that responsibility. The structure, labels, and ordering remain the same for every role.
+
+## Canonical path contracts
+
+The following operator paths are release contracts and are checked against the XML menu tree:
+
+```text
+Federation > Competitions > Seasons
+Federation > Competitions > Season Competitions
+Federation > Competitions > Competition Operations > Create Competition
+Federation > Competitions > Competition Operations > Competition Overview
+Federation > Competitions > Competition Operations > Registration Desk
+Federation > Competitions > Competition Operations > Format Studio
+Federation > Competitions > Competition Operations > Calendar Planner
+Federation > Competitions > Competition Operations > Schedule Planner
+Federation > Competitions > Competition Operations > Schedule Review Queue
+Federation > Clubs & People > Club Directory > Clubs
+Federation > Clubs & People > Club Directory > Teams
+Federation > Match Operations > Match-Day Control
+Federation > Match Operations > Matches
+Federation > Match Operations > Match Sheets
+Federation > Publishing > Approved Schedules
+Federation > Publishing > Schedule Publications
+Federation > Publishing > Standings
+Federation > Finance & Assurance > Finance
+Federation > Finance & Assurance > Compliance
+Federation > Finance & Assurance > Governance
+Federation > Insights > Reports & Insights > Overview & Readiness > Operational Health
+Federation > Administration > Action Queue
+Federation > Administration > System Health > Operational Job Health
+```
+
+## Ownership guidance
+
+- Competition lifecycle records belong under **Competitions**, even when implemented by separate registration, format, calendar, or scheduling addons.
+- Live execution records belong under **Match Operations**. Match-Day Control is intentionally not duplicated under Competitions.
+- Approved output and public visibility controls belong under **Publishing**.
+- Compliance and governance are assurance activities, not system administration.
+- Reports are separated from operational administration to prevent the Administration tab becoming a miscellaneous catch-all.
+- Imports, delivery logs, retention evidence, and background-job recovery remain under **Administration** because they support the platform rather than one business workflow.
+
+## Change checklist
+
+When adding or moving a backend menu:
+
+1. Select its primary operator intent and owning work area.
+2. Place daily actions before configuration and technical records.
+3. Preserve security groups and action access.
+4. Update `docs/COMPETITION_UI_WORKFLOW.md` if the competition journey changes.
+5. Update `ci/check_competition_ui_workflow.py` when a required path or root work area changes.
+6. Run the menu contract check and the affected addon tests.
+

+## Match-day slot generation
+
+Open a draft or capacity-ready match day in **Calendar Planner** and select **Generate Match Slots**. The wizard requests:
+
+- the active venue playing areas to use;
+- the local game-day start and end time;
+- one total slot duration per match;
+- whether a noon pause begins at 12:00 and its duration;
+- whether an existing slot plan may be replaced.
+
+The total slot duration is the complete playing-area occupancy and must include normal play, possible overtime, post-match clearance, and setup for the next match. There is no separate hidden buffer that could make the published times misleading.
+
+The preview reports playable slots, explicit noon-break rows, and candidates rejected by active venue or playing-area constraint windows. Start, end, and pause times are interpreted in the user timezone and stored as the corresponding UTC instants. Generation preserves those planned times when it creates the rows, including explicit break rows; it does not rebase generated rows onto a playing area's existing timeline. Generation creates only slots that finish inside the requested game-day window. Venue-wide constraints affect every selected playing area; area-specific constraints affect only that area. Existing slots are never overwritten unless the operator explicitly enables replacement. Slot generation is unavailable once scheduling has started.
+

+from odoo import _, api, fields, models
+from odoo.exceptions import ValidationError
+
+
+class FederationMatchdaySlotGenerationWizard(models.TransientModel):
+    _name = "federation.matchday.slot.generation.wizard"
+    _description = "Generate Match-Day Fixture Slots"
+
+    matchday_id = fields.Many2one(
+        "federation.matchday",
+        required=True,
+        readonly=True,
+    )
+    venue_id = fields.Many2one(related="matchday_id.venue_id", readonly=True)
+    court_ids = fields.Many2many(
+        "federation.playing.area",
+        relation="federation_matchday_wizard_playing_area_rel",
+        string="Playing Areas",
+        required=True,
+        domain="[('venue_id', '=', venue_id), ('active', '=', True)]",
+    )
+    start_hour = fields.Float(
+        string="Game-Day Start",
+        required=True,
+        default=9.0,
+        help="First possible match start in the venue's local game-day window.",
+    )
+    end_hour = fields.Float(
+        string="Game-Day End",
+        required=True,
+        default=18.0,
+        help="Every generated slot must finish by this time.",
+    )
+    slot_duration_minutes = fields.Integer(
+        string="Total Slot Duration",
+        required=True,
+        default=60,
+        help=(
+            "Total court occupancy per match. Include regulation play, possible "
+            "overtime, post-match clearance, and setup for the next game."
+        ),
+    )
+    noon_pause = fields.Boolean(string="Pause at Noon", default=False)
+    noon_pause_minutes = fields.Integer(
+        string="Noon Pause Duration",
+        default=60,
+        help="Pause beginning at 12:00 local game-day time.",
+    )
+    replace_existing_slots = fields.Boolean(
+        string="Replace Existing Slots",
+        default=False,
+        help="Delete existing draft/capacity slots before generating the new plan.",
+    )
+    generated_slot_count = fields.Integer(compute="_compute_preview")
+    blocked_slot_count = fields.Integer(compute="_compute_preview")
+    pause_slot_count = fields.Integer(compute="_compute_preview")
+
+    @api.model
+    def default_get(self, field_names):
+        values = super().default_get(field_names)
+        matchday = self.env["federation.matchday"].browse(
+            self.env.context.get("default_matchday_id")
+        )
+        if matchday:
+            values.update(
+                {
+                    "matchday_id": matchday.id,
+                    "court_ids": [
+                        (
+                            6,
+                            0,
+                            matchday.venue_id.playing_area_ids.filtered("active").ids,
+                        )
+                    ],
+                    "start_hour": matchday.default_day_start_hour,
+                    "slot_duration_minutes": matchday.default_slot_duration_minutes,
+                }
+            )
+        return values
+
+    @api.depends(
+        "matchday_id",
+        "court_ids",
+        "start_hour",
+        "end_hour",
+        "slot_duration_minutes",
+        "noon_pause",
+        "noon_pause_minutes",
+    )
+    def _compute_preview(self):
+        generator = self.env["federation.slot.generator"]
+        for wizard in self:
+            wizard.generated_slot_count = 0
+            wizard.blocked_slot_count = 0
+            wizard.pause_slot_count = 0
+            if not wizard.matchday_id or not wizard.court_ids:
+                continue
+            try:
+                plan = generator.plan(
+                    wizard.matchday_id,
+                    wizard.court_ids,
+                    wizard.start_hour,
+                    wizard.end_hour,
+                    wizard.slot_duration_minutes,
+                    noon_pause=wizard.noon_pause,
+                    noon_pause_minutes=wizard.noon_pause_minutes,
+                )
+            except ValidationError:
+                continue
+            wizard.generated_slot_count = len(plan["available"])
+            wizard.blocked_slot_count = plan["blocked_count"]
+            wizard.pause_slot_count = len(plan["breaks"])
+
+    @api.constrains(
+        "start_hour",
+        "end_hour",
+        "slot_duration_minutes",
+        "noon_pause_minutes",
+    )
+    def _check_generation_parameters(self):
+        for wizard in self:
+            if not 0 <= wizard.start_hour < 24 or not 0 < wizard.end_hour <= 24:
+                raise ValidationError(_("Start and end must be valid times of day."))
+            if wizard.end_hour <= wizard.start_hour:
+                raise ValidationError(_("Game-day end must be after game-day start."))
+            if wizard.slot_duration_minutes <= 0:
+                raise ValidationError(_("Total slot duration must be positive."))
+            if wizard.noon_pause and wizard.noon_pause_minutes <= 0:
+                raise ValidationError(_("Noon pause duration must be positive."))
+
+    def action_generate(self):
+        self.ensure_one()
+        if self.matchday_id.slot_ids and not self.replace_existing_slots:
+            raise ValidationError(
+                _(
+                    "Existing slots are present. Enable Replace Existing Slots "
+                    "to continue."

+
+## Automatic club-duty allocation
+
+From **Match Operations → Officiating → Plan Match-Day Officials**, select **Auto-assign Club Duties** for a published match day. The default policy requests four roles per match and assigns all missing roles for that match to one participating club.
+
+The allocator is deterministic and balances the accumulated duty count across eligible clubs. It excludes the two clubs playing the target match. By default it also prefers clubs that have no team playing during the target match window; matches on different courts are treated as concurrent when their published time windows overlap. A configurable fallback can use the least-loaded conflicted club when no non-playing club exists. Disable that fallback when the competition requires a strict non-playing-team rule.
+
+**Preserve existing assignments** is enabled by default. Existing active federation or volunteer referee assignments and existing club duties satisfy their role and are never overwritten. The wizard creates only the missing roles. Duties can be opened immediately for club nomination, or left in draft for operator review.
+

+    def _existing_roles(self, matches):
+        referee_roles = self.env["federation.match.referee"].search(
+            [
+                ("match_id", "in", matches.ids),
+                ("state", "!=", "cancelled"),
+            ]
+        )

+    def _covered_match_ids(self, matches, roles):
+        if not self.preserve_existing_assignments:
+            return set()

+        return {
+            match.id
+            for match in matches
+            if all(role in existing.get(match.id, set()) for role in roles)
+        }

+    @staticmethod
+    def _match_club_ids(match):

+        return {
+            club.id
+            for club in (fixture.home_team_id.club_id, fixture.away_team_id.club_id)
+            if club
+        }

+            first_slot

+            and first_slot.start_datetime < second_slot.end_datetime
+            and second_slot.start_datetime < first_slot.end_datetime

+    def _auto_assign_club_duties(self, matches):
+        roles = self._auto_roles()
+        existing_roles = self._existing_roles(matches)
+        candidate_clubs = matches.mapped("logical_fixture_id.home_team_id.club_id")
+        candidate_clubs |= matches.mapped("logical_fixture_id.away_team_id.club_id")
+        if not candidate_clubs:
+            raise ValidationError(_("No participating clubs are available for duties."))
+        load = {club.id: 0 for club in candidate_clubs}
+        existing_duties = self.env["federation.match.club.referee.duty"].search(
+            [("match_id", "in", matches.ids), ("state", "!=", "rejected")]
+        )
+        for duty in existing_duties:
+            load[duty.club_id.id] = load.get(duty.club_id.id, 0) + 1
+        values = []
+        for match in matches.sorted(lambda item: (item.date_scheduled, item.id)):
+            missing_roles = [
+                role
+                for role in roles
+                if not (
+                    self.preserve_existing_assignments
+                    and role in existing_roles.get(match.id, set())
+                )
+            ]
+            if not missing_roles:
+                continue
+            slot = match.published_slot_id or match.operational_slot_id
+            simultaneous = matches.filtered(
+                lambda other: (
+                    other.id != match.id
+                    and slot
+                    and self._slot_windows_overlap(
+                        slot,
+                        other.published_slot_id or other.operational_slot_id,
+                    )
+                )
+            )
+            playing_clubs = set().union(
+                *(self._match_club_ids(other) for other in simultaneous | match)
+            )
+            opponents = self._match_club_ids(match)
+            eligible = candidate_clubs.filtered(lambda club: club.id not in opponents)
+            preferred = eligible.filtered(lambda club: club.id not in playing_clubs)
+            pool = (
+                preferred
+                if self.avoid_clubs_playing_same_slot and preferred
+                else eligible
+            )
+            if (
+                self.avoid_clubs_playing_same_slot
+                and not preferred
+                and not self.allow_playing_club_fallback
+            ):
+                raise ValidationError(
+                    _("No non-playing club is available for %s.") % match.display_name
+                )
+            if not pool:
+                raise ValidationError(
+                    _("No other participating club can cover %s.") % match.display_name
+                )
+            club = min(
+                pool,
+                key=lambda candidate: (
+                    candidate.id in playing_clubs,
+                    load.get(candidate.id, 0),
+                    candidate.id,
+                ),
+            )
+            for role in missing_roles:
+                values.append(
+                    {
+                        "match_id": match.id,
+                        "club_id": club.id,
+                        "role": role,
+                    }
+                )
+                load[club.id] = load.get(club.id, 0) + 1
+        duties = self.env["federation.match.club.referee.duty"].create(values)
+        if self.open_duties:
+            duties.action_open()
+        return duties

 Draft and change-requested schedules refresh the current calendar fixture pool. Late fixtures appear as unassigned work; stale assignments are flagged and never silently deleted. Pending submissions can be withdrawn, while published corrections use governed replacement revisions.
 
+
+## Multi-division match days
+
+A working schedule covers the complete physical match day, not only the division structure that originally opened the planner. If another division is allocated to the same match day during a governed revision, **Refresh Calendar Fixtures** exposes those fixtures as unassigned work and auto-scheduling includes them in its proposal. Submission remains blocked until every non-bye fixture from every match-day allocation is assigned.
+
+Publication validates the current match-day fixture pool again. If allocations change after review, publication stops and requires a refreshed, complete schedule and a new review instead of silently publishing an incomplete game day.
